This game is pretty freaking amazing.
===Pros===
+Combat is smooth and as satisfying as ever.
+BATMOBILE! (This is a double edged sword)
+Great voice acting
+The biggest and best map, dripping with atmosphere and detail, absoloutely fantastic.
+TONS of playtime! Story took me 20 hours to complete
+Side missions are fantastic; first time I have come back to an Arkham game extensively for the side missions
+Great level design
+The most challenging game yet
+A certain character that appears in your mind...
===Cons===
- BATMOBILE COMBAT. Don't get me wrong, it's awesome, but it's waaaaaaaay overused. It gets to a point where you have to solve puzzles to transport the Batmobile. Fighting endless faceless drones gets tedious, and whilst I enjoy it I believe it was certainly overused. Especially the COBRA missions. It's an unfair and mostly boring game of cat and mouse.
- BOSS FIGHTS. This is the worst part of the game. Arkham City set such a high bar for boss fight standard with fights such as Ra's al Ghul or one of the best boss fights in game history, Mr. Freeze. This game has fights of no such calibre; you'll find yourself just fighting tanks.
- Villains disappoint. Our main villain here is Scarecrow. My main problem is that he's always on the sidelines, never in the action. We virtually never see him in the entire game. There isn't even a final bossfight.. Scarecrow is defeated in a cutscene. Really? And also, the Arkham Knight. Not only could I see the reveal from a mile away, his sudden 'redemption' felt cliche and out of place. What? For the whole game he has been ranting about how he wants to kill Batman. And now suddenly he saves him! Also, more backstory please? Why did he become the Arkham Knight exactly? I fail to see why they didn't let you play the mission where he gets captured by Joker...
- Ending. Holy crap, the ending is unsatisfying as hell. After completing the main story, you need to complete four side missions to unlock the true ending. So I do so, and the ending gets cut off on a cliffhanger! To my anger, I found out I needed to complete ALL content in the game. So I had to do all those boring checkpoint fights, some of which are seemingly impossible when there are turrets, minigunners and dozens of armed guards. But y'know, I could have got past that. But the nail in the coffin for me was the Riddler sidemission. To complete the mission, you need to collect all trophies and complete all riddles. Oh, OK? How many? 252. Are you f--king serious? That is completely unreasonable. I looked up the ending on youtube, and even that didn't give closure or a satisfying ending! Are you serious?
So despite my mini-rant, this is a great game. If I had to rank them, it would be miles ahead of Origins, tied with Asylum and behind City, which is the grandfather of Batman games. So overall, 8/10. Pick this game up.

Review:
Although I think Arkham City was probably the best in the series, this game is pretty close in my opinion.  It's nicer looking, bigger, has more story and has the batmobile.  The Batmobile at first is very hard to drive but you do get used to it and can fly around the city and in challenges easily once you know the quirks to it.  In this game Batman is much faster, stronger, and just seems more badass overall.  There are many side characters you can play as with their own short story mod all which are cool and pretty well done.  The Catwoman parts especially were excellent as well as any parts involving Robin.  During these parts you switch back and forth between both characters seemlessly and is extremely fun.
Its hard to go back to the other games once you're use to the speed (especially while flying) in this game.  However, the main reason this game is not the top of the list, is two reasons: Mainly the batmobile is overused, nearly half the game requires you to use the batmobile to do somewhat repetitive missions, and leading into my 2nd argument, for some boss battles too.  The Boss battles in Arkham City had many of my favourite moments in that game but here most of them either use the Batmobile or feel like a "challenge mode" scenario more than a boss fight.
Hightly recommended either way.  Great story, tonts of fun, also Mark Hamill and Kevin Conroy are back voice acting again.

Admittedly, the only reason I bought Saints Row IV, is because I was too impatient to wait for Grand Theft Auto V. For me, GTA is the epitome of open-world exploration, while Saints Row is the epitome of sand box mayhem, and Saints Row IV pretty much takes what it's good at, multiplies it by a fleet of alien space ships, throws a handfull of super powers at it, and sets the whole pile of crazy on fire using an assortment of donuts found at least 2 streets back from your mum's house.
It didn't have the immersion I was pining to get out of a session of GTA, but it did have all the sand box freedom I used to enjoy in my lego sets. I played the game from start to end without ever growing particularly attached to my character or the trials she went though, but the supporting cast was funny and entertaining (and a hell of a lot more interesting than the main plot), and the super powers were a lot of fun to exploit for as long as my progression bar supported...well, progression.
I wouldn't list me as a fan, but I had a good time, and can recommend it to anyone who likes their sandboxes to be full of lasers and dubstep.

The color portion for the strategy does do a reasonable job of keeping things interesting, and the units differences do help in terms of keeping things interesting enough. While the level design needed a bit more variety then it gave, it was able to make up for it with some good music and some good animations. While the game is a port of the iOS version (which despite the fact is “Free” on the store, it's a demo and you have to pay for it), it's reasonable controls despite some quirks. It's good basic strategy fun, although if you're looking for high levels of strategy: you're not going to get it here, as there's a limit to its tricks. Look, it's not going to blow you away, it's a game that's 5 dollars. But you do seemingly get bang for your buck.

Only 3 hours or so of gameplay and I'm absolutely in love with the game. Some pro's and con's are listed below:
Pro's:
- The game's intuitive questing system provides enough guideline to get you fully started and initiated into the game. There's no guessing as to what to do!
- The RPG aspect of the game is wonderful. Full of crafting, fighting, surviving, etc. It's truly a sandbox
- Interface is fairly easy to understand
- Leveling system (though, there is no skill allocation)
- Minimal controls! 1 - 8 on your keyboard, 4 buttons to access your crafting, building, inventory and map, and your mouse.
- Graphics are outstandingly wonderful for the minimalization of spec's required to play the game. Truly is wonderful and simple for any computer or toaster :)
Con's:
- Aerial view can be discomforting at times
- No option to scroll in and out of your character
- All mobs aggro to you, and there's no getting away (But are level 1 when you start, so you can kill them, but 1 by 1)
- A bit of a slow start. So if you're looking to jump in and craft some crazy armor, you're gonna have to wait a bit. (THAT's JUST A PERSONAL THING FOR ME!!!)
Overall - The con's do not nearly have enough of a negative effect on the expereince of the game to say this game is just not amazing. There are very few games out there where you can just play alone and feel like you're immersed into the world. It's your village, your way, your own farms, your own way of fighting, your way for gathering, your way of getting by. You're not restricted by any means and it's just so simply complex. It really is worth the money 100%, and it's developers are certainly headed towards a wonderful future for this fresh RPG Sandbox.
There aren't games as freeing as this folks, so if you're really looking for a, dare I say, realistic Minecraft, or Medeival and simple Elder Scrolls combo, this is definitely the game for you. I'm sure the developers will work with the aerial view and the minor kinks of the game to bring out the best.
Personal Rating: 10/10

Not sure what the hubbub is about.  For all the hyperbole about "OOOH IT'S SO MINDBENDING", Antichamber is actually pretty straightforward, and quite frankly, dull.
Early on, the game has nothing to offer but a handful of obvious tricks, which you'll see through immediately.  At one point the game recreates  the Lost Woods from Ocarina of Time (NON-EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY GUYZ).  I'm not sure why a puzzle game with absolutely no consistency is a good idea,  because it ultimately boils down to futzing around until something new happens.  I was expecting some kind of puzzle game where the laws of  physics/reality are altered in some way, but Antichamber is really a set of disjointed illusions for the first hour, until you get the BLOCK GUN.
Upon finding the block gun, the "mindbending" aspects of the game vanish entirely and lead to an endless series of boring block puzzles.  There's  really nothing particularly clever, challenging, or interesting going on here.  Some of the early block puzzles are alright, but it quickly gets  out of hand.  One "puzzle" literally has you soaking up zillions of blocks to build a giant staircase like some boring version of minecraft.  It's  just tedium.
Most of this is just mediocre, but Antichamber really becomes offensive when all the frustrating parts become apparent.  The dangers of having a game centered on changing the rules and warping reality jump out at you when you realize you're missing crucial information.  Here we have a game that challenges you to "accomplish the impossible", and ironically it's impossible to tell what IS possible.  You'll spend 10 minutes on one puzzle only to discover that some puzzles are literally unsolvable without some new gadget.  I get that the game is meant to be exploratory and somewhat confusing, but some things are explained upfront, and other things are never made clear.
There's very little consistency to the puzzle design.  When a game's design depends on unintuitive logic, the challenge usually comes from discovery: observing cause-and-effect relationships so that you can extrapolate the mechanics.  Antichamber fails because the puzzles are solved upon the first observation, and since there's no consistent puzzle design, the player just stumbles along without having learned anything.  Unfortunately, the lack of direction is compounded by the winding and open-ended nature of the level design.  There's really no obvious path to follow, so you spend a lot of time hitting dead-ends, never knowing whether you're missing something, too thick  to figure out the solution, or need some new ability.
And the levels branch a LOT as you move along, especially early on when you're exploring everything for the first time.  Things tend to close off  behind you, so after you pass by a dozen points-of-interest/corridors, your mental "come-back-to-this" list is overloaded.  It doesn't help that Antichamber is visually quite bland.  Yes, the screenshots on the store page make it look very cool, as if the game were built in Matlab, but 90% of it consists of blank, white, square corridors.  Rare splashes of color don't add much and don't distinguish different areas.  Every door is identical.  Wandering around and backtracking become doubly irritating when the "map" is inconsistent, sometimes showing you places you should explore, but not always.  Thus you'll spend a lot of time aimlessly wandering around trying to figure out where to go next.
The irritations don't stop there.  Traveling around almost always requires you to re-solve the same annoying puzzles again and again, many of which use the equally annoying block gun.  Even worse, Antichamber has an irritating habit of warping you to some other part of the game without warning, often forcing you to teleport again to an earlier area and re-solve the same boring puzzles once more.  Again, I get that the game is supposed to be confusing, but there comes a point where it's no longer for the sake of challenge.
On top of it all, there's really no ultimate goal or progression.  There's no plot or any real sense of place.  For a standard puzzle game, I normally wouldn't complain, but Antichamber is definitely reaching for something more.  There's some real effort put into the sound design.  The ambiance mostly involves odd nature soundscapes; sometimes it works but generally feels out-of-place for a game that is otherwise totally abstract.  The game also loves to bask in its own stupidity with truly awful morsels of wisdom it feeds you constantly.  In many ways, Antichamber feels like it's aiming for Portal a bit too much, including some blatant puzzle mechanics lifted directly.
In the end, I really can't recommend Antichamber.  I think some folks are too easily impressed by a few, admittedly unusual, cheap tricks.  Just play Portal.  Or The Stanley Parable.  Or Echochrome.  Or anything else, really.

Almost every puzzle game has the same overaching goal: solve the puzzles in each area to advance to the next area until you reach the end of the game. The devil is in the details in how each game puts its own unique spin on that theme.
It's difficult to put into words exactly what Antichamber is like, but that's one of the aspects of it that makes it so great. The best way to learn about it is to experience it for yourself. All you have to do is open doors and activate other things by placing blocks. Clues are given to you via riddles on black and white posters with charming little sketches. Sounds simple, right? It is very challenging at times, which is one of the criteria that every puzzle game enthusiast has for a good puzzle game.
The graphics are minimalistic, and yet that never seems like a detriment to the game. If anything, it focuses the attention on the content of the puzzles. If the puzzles weren't that great, that would be a very bad thing. But the puzzles are very, very good. Some parts of the game are so clever they'll have you sitting back in your chair, laughing and shaking your head. I'm sure everyone who has ever played this game has said "wow" aloud at least once during their playthrough of it.
The "rooms" of the game are very surreal. One element attributable to this is the incorporation of infinite loops: you can leave a room through a certain way and end up right back in that room. A word is never spoken during the game, and sometimes the only sound you will hear is the infernal tick-tocking of a swinging pendulum. Going back to the graphics, the lack of detailed texturing actually creates a very cool effect: the game is
artistic. I've realized that you could take a screenshot of almost
in the game, and it would make for a pretty nice piece of artwork. How many games can you say that about? It's like you get to wander through an abstract art museum while solving puzzles.
This game is an experience. There is no other game quite like it. When I think of the most uniquely executed games I've ever played, Antichamber is at the top of my list.

Each tool has a specific function but extracts oil of varying amounts and each is maintained and used via 'mini-games.' After extracting the oil from an island, you sell it on a market that is constantly fluctuating in price and complete challenges that allow you to move from island to island. The tutorial does a great job at explaining how each machine works and how the game is played. Aesthetically, the game is cool, relaxing and has a very peaceful calm demeanour about it... This game is like the unfinished version of the first SW. It copies most things from the old game and invents a single new idea of one "free to explore"-map. This idea combined with the technical problems breaks the game, therefore my advice is:
STAY AWAY FROM THIS GAME!
(Btw, dunno why i spent 12 hours on this, maybe i searched for "something" good in this game, but well, couldve played it through in 8 hours or less...)
+ RPG Part -> Copy from SW1
Skill/Perk system is not very complex but functional, various paths can be used for skilling the characters. The different paths lead to a slightly different gameplay approach. Could be more complex, but works nice and is motivating.
- Fighters and Equipment
On of the highlights in the first game, is now one of the problems. The "natural" progress is gone, you will start with Tier2, grind around some time and -tada- then you will be Tier 4. Natural progress? NOPE.
- Combat
You would expect this to be the same as in SW1, but you have more KI problems, less designed missions and nearly no enemies. Boring.
- Story
There is nothing you can call story. Just some "main missions" without any sense. They look like the random missions. Not much difference. You cant compare this to SW1, it had WAY better missions and story.
- Presentation and Controls
Still like the old but way more problematic...
- Bugs
Way more problems then SW1 - For me personaly it only crashed one time but had alot of KI bugs - Funny as the space is nearly empty compared to SW1...
---Free galaxy
A system you can freely explore sounds good? Well, if all sub-systems are nearly empty its just plain bad. Usually 1 trading station (buy/sell gear/fighters) and 0-2 other stations per subsystem (they are only used for the random missions). If you are lucky also 1 trader or a wing of fighters. But usually all subsystems are empty...
Still you have to fly around for this stupid random missions. There are only 3 types: Patrol, Destroy and Deliver. The involved subsystems are always random. For example, after you take the mission in a trading station:
-> Fly to subsystem XY to start the mission(= you have to cross X maps usually without enemies)
-> Mission is started, fly to subsystem YZ and kill/patrol/deliver (= again X maps, sometimes with a single random attack)
-> If its kill/patrol, you now get your random encounter (you dont even need your figthers, mothership is way to strong)
-> Go back to subsystem XY for reward (OMG).
The good? thing, some of this missions (without enemies, just long, boring travel on empty maps) give 500k, so you go on highest tier pretty fast...

Arkham Knight was meant to be the grand finale to the Arkham games, I expected a lot from this game as I'm a huge fan of these games and Batman in general. But honestly Arkham Knight is...dissapointing. It doesnt live up the hype it built up story wise but in terms of gameplay its the best Arkham game (if you can get past the terrible optimization on PC). The combat systems the best its ever been, gliding and grappling have not felt any better but Arkham Knights biggest new element to gameplay also ends up being its worst. The Bat Tank , I'm not gonna lie...its really cool when you first get to drive around in it but its downhill from there, about 4 or 5 tank battles into it you will realize how stale it gets...shoot a specific number of tanks here, dodge the occasional shot, shoot at enemy tank, rinse and repeat. It gets boring so quick it just ends up being a chore halfway through the game. They should've just kept the tank battles to a minimum instead of making them half of the game. The story isnt all that great in my opinion either, for the game that was supposed to be the last Arkham game the story just isnt  that good...***SPOILERS AHEAD*** I was sorely dissapointed to learn that the Akrham Knight was Jason Todd...it felt so obvious I thought they wouldnt make it Jason but nope Rocksteady went the predictable route. Now the elephant in the room...the PC optimization, its still terrible , probably better than when it launced but honestly I think I could count on one hand how many times my computer managed to run this at 60 fps. With all that in mind I wouldnt recommend Arkham Knight on PC to anyone unless you're a pretty big Batman fan, if you have the option get in console you'll probably have a better experience there.

The game is great! Sure its got mediocre graphics but they're not the highlight anyway. Progression is in these crafting survival games and this game has it in spades! Each upgrade is an obvious increase to your survivability. The only two "survival" stats are health and stamina, neither of which are difficult to manage and death only results in a few items being lost (a permadeath mode can be unlocked it seems). Seeing your base go from a shack and a fire to a spiked fortress filled with animals is incredibly fun and Ill be coming back to this one for a while.
Something that does need to be mentioned is the controls take a bit of getting used to. You are set on a high third person camera right behind your character which is very jarring (even possibly annoying) at first. Holding space allows you to pick stuff up with the mouse or interact with items which feels very "stop and start" since you control the turning of your character when not holding space. This would be a pretty big con EXCEPT you can just hit ctrl to grab stuff. At this point I'm completely used to it and find the controls to be fine.

Admittedly, the only reason I bought Saints Row IV, is because I was too impatient to wait for Grand Theft Auto V. For me, GTA is the epitome of open-world exploration, while Saints Row is the epitome of sand box mayhem, and Saints Row IV pretty much takes what it's good at, multiplies it by a fleet of alien space ships, throws a handfull of super powers at it, and sets the whole pile of crazy on fire using an assortment of donuts found at least 2 streets back from your mum's house.
It didn't have the immersion I was pining to get out of a session of GTA, but it did have all the sand box freedom I used to enjoy in my lego sets. I played the game from start to end without ever growing particularly attached to my character or the trials she went though, but the supporting cast was funny and entertaining (and a hell of a lot more interesting than the main plot), and the super powers were a lot of fun to exploit for as long as my progression bar supported...well, progression.
I wouldn't list me as a fan, but I had a good time, and can recommend it to anyone who likes their sandboxes to be full of lasers and dubstep.

XCOM: EU is a great modernization of the original game. The tension and the difficulty are still there but with improved visuals and ideas. You will need several playthroughs to learn the correct strategies and make the most of the playstyle that suits you. You can easily spend a huge amount of time on that game with a great sense of reward. A must-buy for strategy fans, whether they played the 1994 classic or not. Sadly, the weak point is the lack of diversity in the maps. If a procedurally generated map system may not have worked, a level editor and the steam workshop would have been a match made in heaven. Of course, the Enemy Within expansion adds more diversity, but not that much and kinda breaks the game for me. In EU, the difficulty resided in the fact that the alien were far more advanced and vicious up to the last part (and only if if you did some grinding). In EW, the new units (genetic mod or mechanical ones) are over-powered compared to the feeble new ennemies the extension adds. Still, there are welcome additions (the canadian mission for instance) but it just feels too easy compared to EU. Even with the fine tuning to handicap yourself, something has been lost in the way. I can only recommend Enemy Within to those who really need more of this game and I can truly get that. Others can still enjoy the core game, who is just near-perfect as it is

Ok, so I've read through the negative comments and I think the reason some people are giving bad reviews is because they think the game is too random. What they do not understand is that this game is BASED off of dice rolls. There is a lot of chance involved with this game and the people who gave it bad reviews don't understand that. It's what you are paying for when you get this game and I understand if you don't like it, but don't hate on it for what it is, because it is a really good game.
Ok, now for why you might want to try this game. It does in fact involve a lot of strategy despite what others may say. The difference between a great FTL player and a good one is someone's ability to make the best of what they have even if they are getting the worst rolls imaginable while playing. I used to quit and restart all the time whenever I lost because I was just trying to get the best run possible, but that's not how you learn and get better. There will be runs where the RNG is determined to get you to lose, but for all the people that say the game is based JUST off of chance, let me remind you about all the micro managing, all the decisive choices you must make on what systems to upgrade so you can be the most effective in a fight, and knowing what to do in any combat situation even when the times look dark.
Enough rambling. This is a fantastic strategy game with some rogue like elements, and I hope anyone who has had their interest about FTL peaked and you should check out the game online or maybe even buy it now because it's on sale. It really is a fantastic game and if you buy it now, you get the expansion that comes out early 2014 that adds a type C to all the ships and a new playable race, and a whole bunch of stuff.

Antichamber is a brain-teasing first-person puzzle game set in a minimalistic, zen environment. Every time you play the game, you appear in this central room with the map of the game and settings. You can come back here any time with a push of the Escape key, and teleport to areas in the map you already went to. Within the mazey map are many signs that teach lessons in life after you complete a task resembling the fact. This sign is saved on a wall in the hub and you may choose to reveal all of them, but they are all not required to beat the game.
Antichamber has some of the most unique puzzles I have ever played. The actions are innovative and I enjoyed every bit of it. There is also zen ambience as you venture through the maze, which doesn't get me aggravated as I'm solving puzzles. It's the perfect puzzle mix. There are also guns which you can find in the maze that allow you to shoot blocks. These guns will help you navigate through the rooms. Some later guns have more useful abilities, and the last gun is required to reach the ending. Finally, my absolute favorite part about the game is the countdown timer. I was in the hub when the final seconds went down. Then I found a sign saying "Live on your own watch, not on someone else's". I had a good laugh with it as I was worried this whole game was on a time limit.
I give this game 8/10. It's an innovative puzzle game with a relaxing atmosphere and abstract map design. Best puzzle game I played. I have beaten the game just today, now I should get those remaining signs and complete the map!

As easy as it would be to have a complete stranger guide you through your life and tell you what is correct and what is not, you don't let them because life is about making mistakes and finding solutions. This game parallels that in so many regards. It guides you through a story that only you can narrate, it helps you learn and gives you direction, but not once does it allow you to take advantage an glide right through. The game offers constant challenges and forces the questioning of what you are doing. Insanely hard...but also insanely good.  This is the type of game you can play for 30 seconds or 30 minutes.  If the tight controls and vibrant colors don't make you want to buy this game (and come on, you should, it's VERY cheap), then the incredible chiptune/electronica soundtrack most definitely will.  And if you thought the first stage was impossible, then guess what?  You're not even close to done.  There's five more hair-pullingly difficult stages after that, but the music...oh, jeez, the music...it's gonna keep you coming back for more, trust me.  Despite the crazy difficulty of this game, I never quit it because of how much of a visual and audible spectacle it was every single time I played it.  And that's what insanely hard games like this need: an addicting hook that keeps you wanting to play no matter how hard it gets.  And when I say this game is hard, I mean that one playthough could last anywhere from one second to thirty, depending on how good your reflexes are.  It's THAT hard...and that's only the first stage.  But if you're like me, you won't play this for the difficulty.  You'll play it for the vibrant lights and killer sound.  Pick this up.  Now.

I've never had reason to write a review before.
You need this game.  Consitently, from its first moment to its last, it engages your assumptions and expectations in a way that opened my eyes to the potiental of video games as a medium.  Even through a relatively simple mechanic of interaction with the environment - i.e laying blcoks down and picking them up - it cultivates a very real sense of agency for the player.
The game is not linear at all, in fact most of my difficulties happened because I was trying to do some puzzles before I had the rescources to do them. The paths branch off in all directions, and there are multiple ways into nearly every room. Each puzzle teaches you specific aspects of the rules, with later puzzles and abilites building and expanding on those lessons. All of this happens in a place where the laws of physics and spacial reality do not apply. I've had lots of my friends try playing this game, its crazy to see how differently they approach things.
My favorite part of the game though is how you create the narrative for yourself.  I felt like I was unraveling a crazy, Lost style conspiracy complete with mysterious "radical other."
Don't take my word for it, put a tab on your tounge, buy this game, and grow
For the price that the game is given I find that it is very worth it. Though the experience is better with friends I have found that I can still have much fun with it by myself.

I used to think that this game was terrible and a huge waste of money, but I recently had a change of heart. I guess I thought that this game was going to be like Antichamber when I first saw it, so I bought it. I then got stuck on the very first level and had to use a walkthrough because I thought it was confusing. I didn't really play it very much after I bought it...
One day, I decided to try the level that I was stuck on (Level 02). The level involved using strange board things to get to various areas you could use to recolor the ball. I was just about ready to give up and look up a video walkthrough when I discovered I could
This proved to be one of the main elements I had to use to beat the level, and after that I started to like this game as much as I do Antichamber.
The game always seems to be adding new mechanics constantly, which maintains a nice pace. Every level so far has had at least one thing in it that is different from the previous, which I like a lot.
There is one important thing that I realized when I finally beat Level 02:
This makes perfect sense if you look at certain elements of the game. Unlike Antichamber, there are ways to die in the game. The thing is, though, that you
, which leads to some VERY interesting solutions. Sometimes dying is the only way to solve a puzzle, or, at least, the most obvious way.
I have encountered a few glitches so far. Sometimes a ball will unexplainably warp and stretch if it isn't the right color for a square, which acts kind of like a button in Portal that needs a specific color. If a board falls in lava (Or whatever that red stuff is), it will usually respawn standing straight up. I haven't unlocked any of the acheivements that you get for beating a level yet, even though I am somewhere around Level 05 or 06. For the most part, however, the game is fine. It also runs smoothly on my computer, but that might be from the fact that it has something like 2 graphics cards in it. You can adjust the graphics quality anyway, so that might mean the game could even run on a fairly old computer, provided that the lowest graphics settings could permit that. There isn't really much in the way of graphics, as most of it is putting colored balls into squares. This doesn't bother me, though, as the relatively simple art style helps me focus on the gameplay.
My only real complaint is the soundtrack. I usually play without the sound on, and for (In my opionion) a great enough reason. At one point I randomly decided to turn the game volume up a little bit. I heard a little bit of what I think was a guitar song that carried over to a little bit of the start of the next level. I then heard a completely different-styled song that seemed to be mostly piano. The soundtrack is seemingly incoherent, as I can piece together just from listening to these two completely different-sounding tracks. There isn't any sound in the game other than the soundtrack as far as I can discern, though, so you won't be missing out on any important audio clues by having the game's sound turned off.
All in all, Colortone is a great little game that will reward that certain player that likes to experiment with a game to beat it. It does have a few bugs here and there, but these glitches don't ruin the gameplay for the most part.

The single best zombie game out there.
The gameplay is fantastic. There is great diversity in the weapons that you can choose from, and it's balanced in a way that no other zombie game is. Almost every weapon in the game is useful, so even if your mini chainsaw (the most OP weapon in the game) breaks in the middle of a zombie horde, you can grab that mannequin torso from the nearby clothing store and still be fine. The timer is a fantastic addition, but it's not for everyone. It adds a certain level of stress to the game, however if you're interested in exploring instead of the quests or subquests, just ignore the timer and you'll be fine.
The setting is incredible. This is one aspect that the sequels to this game failed at. DR1 combines seriousness and spookiness with just the right about of silliness. It's a goofy game at times, but at other times there is a very serious horror/drama undertone. I personally think that DR2 and 3 took the silliness to the extreme and ruined the tone of their games.
Overall, I cannot recommend this game enough. As a port it had a few issues at launch, particularly with saving, but I've updated to the latest patch and it runs like a dream. Up to 4k resolutions supported and uncapped FPS. Easily one of the best games of the year, despite being originally released over 10 years ago.

I don't often have the inspiration to write reviews or comments about games, but in this case I kind felt I had to. This game was on my wishlist for a long time and I loved the demo on the Xbox 360; but the word 'clunky' describes Mirror's Edge all too well.
The screenshots and trailers paint a beautiful picture of freerunning across glorious, colourful rooftops with a seamless flow of wall-running, vaulting and ducking leading to extremely satisfying gameplay... But to be quite honest with you, you're going to be spending 60% of your time inside a claustrophobic building with little to no idea on how to progress. Runner vision shows you where your *end* goal should be, but often the frustration of having no clue how to *get* there by far outweighs the satisfaction one receives from actual free-running. When I bought the game I was hoping to be spending most of my time exploring the open-air environment - not stood at the end of a platform, scratching my head on where on earth to go next. Despite the 'next obstacle' often being highlighted in red, I found these areas simply not 'intuitive' enough for me to follow the supposed 'flow' of the game.
As much as the endless swarms of cops is annoying at times, it is rewarding to outmaneuver them through well-timed counters or simple evasion. As stated countless times the game looks fantastic despite being five years old, and the concept of Mirror's Edge itself is unique and very promising. The game sometimes rewards good intuition and reaction times in flying your way through the missions; but these moments are so few and far between that it causes the story mode to come as a bit of a disappointment. Time Trials soften the blow but do not heal it.
All in all I guess I just felt slightly let down after all the images the trailers and screenshots painted in my head, and the story itself doesn't act as a consolation by any means. If you've been dying to play this game for a long time, then go right ahead and you'll probably find it unique and interesting - but if you're browsing through games here or there and you happen to give this one a miss, it's certainly not going to be the end of the world.

XCOM: EU is a great modernization of the original game. The tension and the difficulty are still there but with improved visuals and ideas. You will need several playthroughs to learn the correct strategies and make the most of the playstyle that suits you. You can easily spend a huge amount of time on that game with a great sense of reward. A must-buy for strategy fans, whether they played the 1994 classic or not. Sadly, the weak point is the lack of diversity in the maps. If a procedurally generated map system may not have worked, a level editor and the steam workshop would have been a match made in heaven. Of course, the Enemy Within expansion adds more diversity, but not that much and kinda breaks the game for me. In EU, the difficulty resided in the fact that the alien were far more advanced and vicious up to the last part (and only if if you did some grinding). In EW, the new units (genetic mod or mechanical ones) are over-powered compared to the feeble new ennemies the extension adds. Still, there are welcome additions (the canadian mission for instance) but it just feels too easy compared to EU. Even with the fine tuning to handicap yourself, something has been lost in the way. I can only recommend Enemy Within to those who really need more of this game and I can truly get that. Others can still enjoy the core game, who is just near-perfect as it is

A very good strategy game that runner-up for numerous strategy game of the year awards, second only to X-COM.
You manage a ship containing crew members and try to survive till the last sector. There is a huge variety of alien race available as crew members with their strengths and weaknesses.
Your ship can also have a variety of weapons like beams, missiles, drones, even a teleporter that allows you to beam your crew members to the enemy ship to try and take it by brute force.
You also have to balance your ship's power to support various rooms like oxygen, shields, weapons, and cloaking. This also means there are many ways to defeat your enemies other than destroying it, such as burning them out with fire, and depriving them of oxygen.
The only con is that this game is random, and what weapons or crew members you can get depends on luck. Most of the time you cannot get your ideal setup. But the game allows unlockable ships which start out in a certain way. So that alleviates the randomness a bit.
A must-buy for strategy game fans.

I've never had reason to write a review before.
You need this game.  Consitently, from its first moment to its last, it engages your assumptions and expectations in a way that opened my eyes to the potiental of video games as a medium.  Even through a relatively simple mechanic of interaction with the environment - i.e laying blcoks down and picking them up - it cultivates a very real sense of agency for the player.
The game is not linear at all, in fact most of my difficulties happened because I was trying to do some puzzles before I had the rescources to do them. The paths branch off in all directions, and there are multiple ways into nearly every room. Each puzzle teaches you specific aspects of the rules, with later puzzles and abilites building and expanding on those lessons. All of this happens in a place where the laws of physics and spacial reality do not apply. I've had lots of my friends try playing this game, its crazy to see how differently they approach things.
My favorite part of the game though is how you create the narrative for yourself.  I felt like I was unraveling a crazy, Lost style conspiracy complete with mysterious "radical other."
Don't take my word for it, put a tab on your tounge, buy this game, and grow

Killing Floor 2 is a first-person cooperative horde survival game with excellent replayability and a very fun level progression system.
-The graphics are fantastic, since the devs are using a heavily modified version of Unreal Engine 3. Seriously, this game looks like Unreal Engine 4. In fact, I originally thought that this game used Unreal Engine 4 from the get-go, but I was wrong.
-The maps look like locations you'd actually see in real life. They're very well-crafted, and you can see that they put thought into each one.
-Gameplay is fun and engaging. It demands your full attention and rewards you for playing smart. With both a high skill ceiling, and friendlier, more relaxed difficulties too, this game can be enjoyed by anyone who likes this genre. Warning: The game can be frustrating as all get-out if you're playing on harder difficulties if you aren't being alert. Also, on the harder difficulties, the bosses can be a real pain to bring down too.
With continued updates, and the workshop modding, this game is a gift that'll keep on giving.

Sometimes I wish there was a "Kind of" option on the reccomendations.
Mirror's Edge is a brilliant idea executed poorly. It is exciting and immersive gameplay hindered by terrible level design.
Let's start with the positives.
---The gameplay. This alone would be worth buying for, which is why I still have a "yes" as my reccomendation. The fact is, it is a great experience running around in Faith's body. And the few times when the level design is great, it is unbeatable.
---The music. I enjoyed the music. It was good enough to fuel the energy of the game but wasn't too much that it distracted you from it. Exactly how game music should be.
---The scenery. The city is beautiful. Not much more to say here. Just major props for a beautiful background.
The negatives.
---Level design. This is my main gripe about the game. You are in a parkour/freerunning game. You want to be able to flow. You want to be able to run. There just wasn't any flow. Don't get me wrong. There were moments. However, the entire story is about the runners and how the are good at running. Except, because of the level design, you don't really get to show that off. You get to jump from a rooftop or two, then you are back to climbing on some wall or sitting in an elevator for 2 minutes or trying to get some weird wall run that makes no sense.
--The story. Snore. Cheesy. Cliched. Illogical. Basically it sucks. While the animation was nice, thats about all that it had. The story was bad and the dialouge was bad.
--Combat. Major downside of this game. It is the same thing as the freerunning. Great concept, terribly executed. The great ideas was to have a cool martial art disarm system. However, actually doing this in-game was a chore. You have to wait for the enemies guns to turn red, which you really don't want to care about in battle. Also, it was actually pretty hard to do. Which sucks in rooms with more than two enemies because if you don't get it right the first time you are going to die.
--Lack of open world. This annoyed me. There is no openess to a game that needed it most. At most, you might get two paths, that aren't really even two paths. Its just deciding to jump over a fence or jump over a box. Huge failure here on EA's part.
--The ending. Not going to spoil it. But it sucked.
Conclusion:
You see how many hours I've put into this game? Its probably going to stay like that. I had to uninstall the game to make room on my computer, and frankly, I have no plans to ever reinstall it again. I finished the story. I did some of the time trials. I've had my fill. So I guess thats my conclusion. It was good enough to finish. And that's about it. Let's hope the sequel is better.

Ok, so I've read through the negative comments and I think the reason some people are giving bad reviews is because they think the game is too random. What they do not understand is that this game is BASED off of dice rolls. There is a lot of chance involved with this game and the people who gave it bad reviews don't understand that. It's what you are paying for when you get this game and I understand if you don't like it, but don't hate on it for what it is, because it is a really good game.
Ok, now for why you might want to try this game. It does in fact involve a lot of strategy despite what others may say. The difference between a great FTL player and a good one is someone's ability to make the best of what they have even if they are getting the worst rolls imaginable while playing. I used to quit and restart all the time whenever I lost because I was just trying to get the best run possible, but that's not how you learn and get better. There will be runs where the RNG is determined to get you to lose, but for all the people that say the game is based JUST off of chance, let me remind you about all the micro managing, all the decisive choices you must make on what systems to upgrade so you can be the most effective in a fight, and knowing what to do in any combat situation even when the times look dark.
Enough rambling. This is a fantastic strategy game with some rogue like elements, and I hope anyone who has had their interest about FTL peaked and you should check out the game online or maybe even buy it now because it's on sale. It really is a fantastic game and if you buy it now, you get the expansion that comes out early 2014 that adds a type C to all the ships and a new playable race, and a whole bunch of stuff.

Enjoyment of this game is going to be REALLY dependent on either your threshold for bull**** or your nostalgia. This is one of those games that is traditionally considered "hardcore" like Demons Souls and Battletoads. It is 100% unforgiving of your mistakes, and even small errors can net you a huge loss in progress.
BUT.
If you are willing to let the game punish you for your errors, you will find that the lessons it teaches you will ultimately cause you to fall in love with its hardcore quirkiness. Since it was practically a launch title, it feels like a game designed for the PS2 that had extra horsepower to play with. The animations, and the janky "gaminess" of it all, is all set to the backdrop of a SUPER well realized fictional mall that, for all the years I have been playing this game, has never ceased to amaze me with how its aesthetic and audio tone feels 100% authentic. The crowd tech that powers this is obviously inferior to that of later Dead Rising games, but they designed the game to minimize the showing of those limitations. Obviously on PC at higher resolutions these limitations become a little more obvious, but when you're wading through a swarm of smoothly animated zombies all clustering and clawing at you and you can see them in the distance huddling over and chowing on a psychopath or survivor that just died... it just feels so authentic and cool.
The reason why I think I can forgive how hard this game is is the simple fact that you keep your character progress between games. So you can fail as much as you like, but you will always be making at least a little progress.
As you can see from my playtime and my achievements, I am REALLY into this game (having unlocked a lot of the hardest  ones in a cluster), because once I gave myself in to its flaws, I have never since been able to replicate the feeling it has given me. The closest would probably be Red Dead Redemption, but I have strong doubts we'll ever see that come back. :(
Some things I must address, though, in the interest of full disclosure, is that it has some REALLY strong flaws that may make you smash something (maybe even something expensive). For one, AI is TERRIBLE all around, the only reason that bosses are as hard as they are is because they clearly have superpowers and the game pretty much clears all zombies from the area that you fight in so they are a non-issue for most bosses. Plus, they have incredibly powerful weapons that are always guaranteed to take off a significant amount of health. Some of them even have insanely high defense to even the most powerful of weapons and can block almost all attacks, leaving TINY windows of oppotunity that only the most hardcore players of this game will be able to take advantage of. For survivors, the AI makes them do INCREDIBLY STUPID S***. ON YOUR FIRST PLAYTHROUGH YOU WILL LOSE SURVIVORS TO THEIR OWN STUPIDITY LIKE THEM GETTING IN THE WAY OF YOUR ATTACKS, RUNNING DIRECTLY INTO A SWARM OF ZOMBIES, AND NOT BEING ABLE TO DEFEND THEMSELVES IF GRABBED. TAKE IT FROM THE GUY THAT LITERALLY SAVED EVERY POSSIBLE SURVIVOR. THEY ARE INFURIATINGLY DUMB. My advice? Carry queens (essentially grenades that only affect zombies) at all times, and carry food. Also, if you can equip them with shotguns, DO IT.
The second huge thing that may put people off is the time limit. The whole game runs on a universal time limit, and essentially the game is 6 in-game hours long (8-9 if you do the first 6 perfectly). Everything that can happen in the main story of the game happens in that 6 hours, and everything is always counting down but it never tells you SPECIFICALLY when a mission will expire. On your first playthrough, you may have to sacrifice survivors to get through more story missions.
The third huge issue you may have is death is unforgiving. If you have not been diligently saving your progress, you WILL lose all story/side mission/achievement progress since you last remembered to save. This is going to be a hard lesson to accept at first but THANKFULLY the character progress transfer is there. That last fact is why I could stand all the difficulty this game threw at me.
All my own personal reasons aside (I swear I could make a thesis out of this), I have two reasons why I hope you will buy this game right now, sale or no sale.
1) To support developers going through their backlogs and porting their games over to the one, truly sustainable platform that will guarantee their games can be enjoyed for generations to come.
2) I honestly feel this is a landmark game for the 360/PS3 generation onwards, it did zombies and it did zombies RIGHT before the market became saturated with them.
If you have a penchant for games that will not hold your hand and force you to earn their endings, this is a must-have. I feel this game gives me almost endless replayability, and whether that's nostalgia or whether this game may really be that good? I can't objectively say. What I can say is, there really isn't anything like this out there anymore.
PRO TIP: Get the "Zombie Genocider" achievement (it's easier than you think, it's mainly just time consuming) before making a real run at the game. You'll see why.
EDIT: I now have all the achievements. Am I a hardcore gamer now?

Minimalistic games are usually minumalistic because the designers/programmers are cutting corners and calling it "artsy;" however, Antichamber's minimalism is a deliberate choice to make the programming and design tricks much less obvious and much more powerful.
The game very effectively creates a world in which the player's understanding of reality needs to be recreated since very little will make sense at first. It's a world where the law of gravity is the only one that is obeyed, and non-Euclidean geometries have their way with the fabric of reality. There are no enemies, but there is one massive, immersive, and psychological puzzle that will repeatedly challenge the player inside of the Antichamber.

Colortone is an interesting Puzzle Adventure Indie game where you use colors to solve different puzzles. I will provide a TL;DR at the end.
Currently there are 14 (15 if you include level 0) levels to play through. The first few levels could be seen as tutorials to show you the different features and ways to beat puzzles within the game. Everything within Colortone is linked with using colors, whether it be to finish the level, destroy a wall, or to make a platform. There are 6 colors within Colortone which are the 3 primary colors (blue, red, and yellow) and the 3 secondary colors (purple, orange, and green). There are 2 types of object you can color according to which dab of colour you put it in, a small sphere and a board. You can dip these in individual colors or you can dip in one, then another, to create a secondary color. The game uses an interesting platforming idea where you place your boards on certain colored rods and if the board matches the colored rod then it have created a platform for you to jump on. There are also machines which use the sphere colored with primary colors to create its secondary colors (Example: blue would create green and purple), secondary colors create their individual primary colors (Example: green would create blue and yellow), and a machine which will take the color of the sphere and put it down so you can use it (Example blue means you get blue). There are certainly a lot of good puzzle elements which can be utilized within Colortone to make sure it is a very pleasant experience.
Colortone has an amazing soundtrack that is able to easily ease you into a calm mood to play through and enjoy the game. The graphics are fairly basic, nothing that stand out that much. The game will be mostly white except for the colors seen in walls, platforms, spheres, machines, light beam, and everything you can use/have to go through to beat the level and lava.
+ Good concept
+ Great use of color within puzzles to solve them
+ Good soundtrack
+ Fun gameplay
+ Options for colorblind to allow for them to enjoy this game
- Very limited replay value (only 15 levels)
- Beatable within 2 hours
- Some levels have a slight problem where if you die with an object and lose it, you are unable to obtain it and have to restart
- Unable to run on Windows 10 (at the moment)
These are my personal suggestions to the game that I feel will change the game for the better.
- An in-game editor to allow players to create their own levels along with a sharing feature to play other people's maps
- More campaign maps
I was able to enjoy almost all of my time spent within Colortone, but I was disappointed to find out that there were only 15 levels with nothing else. This game would be drastically improved if it had an editor with the map to create custom maps.
Colortone is a very interesting and fun to play puzzle game that utilizes colors. The game is currently around 2 hours to beat with only 15 levels. The soundtrack does a nice job in immersing you into the game and makes for a more relaxing experience. If you like the look of the game and have the $5 lying around you might consider purchasing this for yourself as it's a good experience with everything that is within the game so far.

Colortone is an amusing little game that combines color mixing with puzzle solving, together these elements bring a fun little concept that's sure to entertain players.
PROS:
+ Stylish, minimalist design; The graphics are simplistic, and with the muted color tone it's also pleasant to look at.
+ Effective concept; the game revolves around mixing colors to progress throughout the levels, and instead of continuously adding more and more stuff the levels develop and build around this single gimmick.
+ Acceptable difficulty for all levels of players; It starts at just the right difficulty and steadily builds up to harder challenges.
+ Enjoyable to fool around with; It's so much fun to mix colors together, and especially to destroy breakable walls with the appropriate color.
CONS:
- No checkpoints...?; Some levels seem to have you respawn at a certain point in the level if you die, while others make you restart all the way back to the beginning. This is problematic as some longer levels make you start over from the beginning.
- Minor glitches; Some objects won't respawn if they fall into a pit of lava, for one. There was also an unusual glitch where a board I was carrying suddenly doubled in length. Like... what?
- Too short: Colortone can be completed in fewer than 2 hours, even less if you know what you're doing.
Overall Colortone is a fun little game, and a nice time-killer when you want to wind down from more intense games.
AFFIRMATIVE

I originally picked this up when I heard about it during the Co-Optional Podcast's releases section when TB mentioned it looked Antichamber-esk. With me being one of the few people who have hundreds of hours in Antichamber (speedrunning/routing), it looked like an obvious game to pick up, and upon buying it (during it's early access period), noticed it had a "Speedrun" mode button on the main menu, which appealed to me. At the time, it wasn't a functional mode, and was just a placeholder button. I livestreamed my first play of the early access version, and promptly posted
on the community discussions what my thoughts were (along with some bugs).
The dev is very nice and responsive in the community discussions, however this is where the game starts to get a few demerits from me. I realize making a game can be time consuming, and plenty of other things can be much more important, but the dev had specifically assigned dates for each new level to come out. This schedule worked fine for the majority of the levels, however near the last few levels, the dev missed releasing about 3 or 4 levels in a row, constituting about 2 months of no updates, with no word from the dev about when updates would come. The only information was via
on the community discussions. The dev also does not maintain any active news/announcements posts or changelogs so when the game does update, you have no idea what has changed, and you can't look back at any "previous" changelogs because none exist.
Mid-August was meant to be the release for the first level that was skipped, and as seen in the thread linked above, the dev said that all the final levels as well as speedrun mode would be finished by the end of September. Nearing the end of October is when the update finally arrived, without speedrun mode, and with two broken levels. The bugged levels were promptly fixed, as I have already said the dev is responsive on the community discussions.
Sure there are bugs, but nothing too major. Any major bugs I've seen (and posted about) have been promptly fixed by the dev. Again, as I said above, the dev is quite responsive for this kind of stuff. The only main bugs I can think of currently are that some objects can get stuck inside walls/floor, but it can be looked at as a quirk of the game and just takes some getting used to how to control yourself when carrying an object. I've found that the controls themselves are fine for my tates, as opposed to what some of the other reviews say about the right/left mouse functions, just takes some getting used to.
There is no information regarding speedrun mode at the time of posting this, and last I checked, the button in the main menu has been removed, and the game has come out of early access, so I feel as though the dev has dropped the idea completely.
$5 is pretty cheap, so I would recommend it, and the game itself as-is right now is still pretty great for that price, however I do feel like there are a lot of things the dev could have done better during the early access time period, such as posting changelogs (or even having version numbers to begin with), or news posts about any delays or changes of ideas/direction.

In this game, you play as Steve Oldboy (or Stephana if you choose female gender)
Trapped in a mind vortex between the apalachian mountains on a trip from france, you find yourself in a strange new place where there are bad guys trying to kill you, and you only want one thing: Revenge. The story is beautifully integrated into the gameplay where you never know if you are stuck in the vortex-coma space or real time. You think you wake up, but waking up was just a dream within the coma (you may find this as hard to follow as inception at times) so you go forth to take your revenge while time is slowing down as it runs out, your "homeboys" backing you up cheering at you to destroy the big bad guy (of which there are several)
Then once you think you can wake up you start walking the streets blasting your brain powers over all the bad people when you realize that you brain powers shouldn't be real, or should they?
There is a twist.
Overall a good game if you keep a notepad and jot down some notes to follow the story.

Actual Review Time  (THIS REVIEW CONTAINS A LITTLE BIT OF SPOILERS FOR THE SCOOPS)
This game...this game.  This is the best game i have ever played.  After 10 whole years...10...years...Im so happy it finally came out on PC.
Gameplay 10/10
The gameplay is FANTASTIC!  It is so much fun to play this game.  So much fun.  There is so many weapons, guns, and more.  Sure some weapons you have to spend hours to get (i.e. laser sword and Mega Buster) but they getting the achievements for them are well worth it.  The laser sword just destroys everything, and the mega buster...well i mean its the mega buster you know what it is.
How Long the Game is
The game lasts as long as you want it too.  What I mean is that there is so many endings (6-7 i think) and scoop chances!  The game is not meant to beaten only once, it is meant to be beaten many many times.  If you want even more to do, try and get all the achievements; I can think of atleast 2 that takes over 20 hours (7 Day Survivor and Zombie Genocider.)  So 20 dollars for at least 50 hours?  Thats more hours than most games!  Its only 20!?
Micro-Transactions and DLC?
Nope.  None.  Thats right, a game that doesn't have MT and DLC.  You spend 20 dollars, and you get the FULL game,  not tiny bits or unfinished story bits.  The FULL game.
Is It a Good Port?
Yes, it is a great port!  The option menu is okay, but it has the essentials (also it is by far, the best Dead Rising port.  The others run like garbage.)  I've seen people running it at 4K, 1440P.  You also do NOT need a beefy PC for this game, a low end will work just fine.  Like 60FPS Ultra fine.  So almost everyone can play it.  NOTE:  SOME PEOPLE HAVE BEEN REPORTING ISSUES LIKE DIRECTX FAILED TO INITALIZE!  I HAVE NOT HAD THESE ISSUES.
Story 8/10
The story was alright.  It had interesting moments and has many memorable scenes.  Whether it is the best story between all the games is debatable.  But no DR has come close to the memorable scenes and characters.
What About DR 2, OTR, and DR 3?
Forget them, Dead Rising 1 is the best out of all of them.  None of them have as great of story, gameplay, or value.  Also!  Dead Rising 1 does not have GAMES FOR WINDOWS LIVE!!!  Dead Rising 2 and OTR do.  DR 3 though is...not great, it is okay but its 10 dollars more than 1 and it is definately not work that extra 10.  The value of getting the Mega Blaster or the Laser Sword is something unmatched by the other 2.  Especially Dead Rising 3, I got the Mega Buster without any difficulty in 3, like it uses the same save stuff from DR1, and thats about it.  You just have to beat the game.  Not that hard.
Common Cons That Are Easily Fixable
Time:  sigh, really the time?  The thing that adds the sence of fear of failure?  Well heres the thing, as long as you dont continue with the "Save Brad Mission" at the beginning of the game, you can do whatever you want.  The game isnt restricted, you dont want to play the story?  Go right ahead.  If the 3 days end, just restart the game.  You still have all your progress (like levels and achievement items.)

This is my review for Fairy Fencer F. The game is a JRPG with multiple endings, node based exploration, visual novel styled conversations, and hidden characters. I enjoyed the game quite a bit but must admit a bias towards the game type; I have all the Neptunia games on both Console and on Steam plus others from Compile Heart enjoy the style that Fairy Fencer F was presented in; a brightly colourful, endearing characters, and wild romp of a game. The game is not entirely happy and cheery, but it would be something I would recommend playing if you want a break from the gritty grim dark edgy genre that is in vogue right now. The game sets out to do the things it is made to do, and it does them well. It does not try to be something it is not, so keep that in mind when purchasing it.
The Good:
The characters are well developed with rational arcs and believable actions and intentions. The story is a heroes journey with some subversions and twists on the trope and is set in a unique post-apocalyptic world. I found it overall an enjoyable one. The graphics are colourful and in the anime style. The main game takes around 20 Hours to complete but there are multiple endings to add on to this, for the price of admission I think this is a fair price. The game has skip functions to speed up battles when grinding and end visual novel sections when replaying, this helps alleviate tedium that other JRPG's fall victim to. Combat is satisfying with abilities and animations are very well done; you can also unlock all kinds of costumes for your characters. The voice acting is delightful and one of the characters has a Canadian accent, which pleased me greatly.
The Bad:
There are some railroad battles where you are meant to fail, even if you manage to defeat the enemy, which I always dislike. Mood whiplash occasionally occurs when the tone shifts rapidly from comical to tragic and back, these moments are few- like the mass graves part. There is excessive grinding to unlock all the powers and reach maximum level, this is not required to beat the game but is required to see all the endings.
The Ugly:
Pippin, seriously what the hell is he?

Possibly one of the worst platformers I've ever played.
Graphically, you're yeah, the cube in the title. Exactly a cube.
The levels are a big background made up by one colour only and the levels are all like this, two rows that you've got to pass since the exit door will always be up above of you.
The music is terribly annoying and the worst thing is that it's a MIDI loop that every time you die starts from the beginning. And you will die a lot. Even on the first level. The first obstacle of the first level.
The hitbox is huge and you'll die thousands of times only while trying to jump between static obstacles.. and then you'll also have monsters and moving obstacles.
In the settings you can choose from windowed or full screen mode, but nothing else. The controls are only WASD and escape, nothing else.
Luckily it's so fast and easy to load that every time you die (as I said, thousands of times per level) you'll instantly respawn (with the music abruptly stopping and re-starting from the beginning), but anyways it becomes frustrating from the first level and there's 24 of them.
I recognize that it's the effort of a single Russian developer (if you go windowed, you'll have a bar on the upper side written only in Russian) but really, 2€ for a game like this is one of the worst things the Steam store could possibly offer in my opinion.
Going back a little bit to the game, as I said it's an extremely basic platformer. Your goal will be to get to the door and when I was talking about the obstacles maybe I have been too quick. It's not that there are few of them, the big problem is that everything is extremely hard to overcome and it seems that really no one has ever tested a single level (by the way, every level will be open from the menu so that you can complete some later levels that are in fact easier than the first ones). You'll have to deal with crosses going up and down at an extreme velocity, or monsters (which are blocks like you, colored in a different way) that run twice fast as you.
It's really frustrating, everything. I'm not saying that it's impossible to play, but really as a platformer I've never seen probably something so badly realized and developed.
And it's also filled with bugs; apart from the hitbox that will make you die by almost being in the zone of everything, some of the static white bars/obstacles allow you to place yourself over them so that you clearly see your character being half over the obstacle, while many of them instantly kill you only by a touch.
I'm not against hard games, although I like the games which 1. allow you to choose a difficulty setting or 2. have an increasing difficulty curve that goes on with your knowledge and accompanies you from the easiest through the hardest levels. But this is beyond hard, it's stupidly hard since it's not meant to be hard, it's so difficult due to the poorly developed system and the insane amount of moving and static obstacles put in every single level.
So, even if you're looking for a hard platformer, I warmly suggest you to avoid this game completely.
I'd like to suggest you some levels (7, 9 or 10 maybe) if you wanna try the "easiest" ones but really, it's utterly frustrating and would not deserve a playthrough even if it was for free, let alone for 2€.

I'd definitely recommend the whole series, but not at full price!

This is a cute little visual novella. It is one of a series of four, that basically are each what in a traditional visual novel is a path. So basically, consider this as having chosen your path first. Sakuya (you can rename her) is a young woman who... does not want to act girly. As such, when offered the chance to be a test subject for her cousin's new attraction for women, she manages to convince him to let her try the other attraction... the one geared towards men. In the first few moments, she finds herself trapped with one of the four other participants. In this title, a young boy named Akio (who isn't really a young boy). Oh, and since she can choose her avatar, she chose to partake as a male.
There are three endings. The bad ending is unlocked if you make a wrong choice (one of which also unlocks an achievement about a carrot). The neutral/friendship ending depends on you choosing the lesser of two choices at the end of a stage. And the good/love ending is the better of those two choices. Oh, and choosing that better one also unlocks a small additional scene for the story (and accompanying CGs).
The game is beautiful, at least for the time. I have a feeling this is one of the first products put out by this publisher, as it is a bit rough around the edges.
Also, my suggestion would be to buy the East Tower Complete Edition. Especially as the last volume is almost three quarters of the price of the bundle...

East Tower-Akio is a fun, otome visual novel made by the same developer as dUpLicity~Beyond the Lies, the developer's first game to make it on Steam. For those who weren't fans of dUpLicity, I can say that East Tower-Akio is very different and in ways, it's an improvement. For one, the art style is better and the faces are more realistic although they are still in the anime style. Also, the writing is more light-hearted but that is no surprise, as the East Tower series takes on a more comedic tone although it has mystery as its main element.
As there are already summaries of the story posted, I won't repeat them. Rather, I'll give what I liked about the game as well as some negatives. I liked how you can pursue two paths here-a friendship and a romance path. On my first playthrough, I went for the friendship path, as I usually reserve the romance paths on my final playthrough. Akio is a serious character but once the MC gets to know who he truly is underneath, I found myself to like him, as he comes to care for the MC in return. So the story itself appealed to me. Also, I liked how it takes place in a virtual reality dreamworld. Although it's not the most original idea, I like the concept of being in a world where you can imagine your dreams becoming reality through sheer willpower. As I mentioned earlier, the art is better as well although it's a personal preference.
As for criticisms, I only have a couple. First, I noticed that there were a few awkward phrases that could have been reworded better. However, as they only appeared in a few lines, this is such a minor criticism. As for the other, this is more of a personal preference but I wasn't a fan of how this game is split into four parts rather than just made into one huge game with four paths. Now I do understand why this was the case but I tend to prefer playing VNs that have all the paths readily available so I can choose which one to play first.
Overall, though, I did enjoy this first game in the series and getting acquainted with the mystery behind East Tower. I can't wait to try out the other paths soon and see how they compare.

This is the way indies should be made. Designed with short play sessions in mind, but with lots of replayability built in.
Mechanics: It' a beat-em up inside a closed arena. Enemies keep spawning until the enemy count for the stage is reduced to zero. Enemy variety is just about right. What'll keep you entertained is learning new skills and switching between them so that Freesia can adapt to a particular stage or boss.
Controls: I used a Logitech F310 Gamepad. It was recognized without a problem and so I configured the controls to my liking. No noticeable input delays.
Story: Princess Mononoke Lite (Man VS Nature). Just the right amount of comedy, drama, and kawaii.
Music: Very soothing and cheerful. If it fails to make you smile, your heart is Valyrian steel.
Stability: I saw a lot of complaints in the forums about the game not launching properly or crashing all the time, but I didn't experience a single hitch during my playthrough. It's possible the bugs have been patched. Good news for latecomers, hehe.
Replayability: Beating the game once unlocks Difficult Mode and Guardian Mode. Beating the game on Difficult Mode unlocks the toughest difficulty. You'll end up repeating the game more than once so you can learn all of Freesia's skills and clock in speedruns.
Price: What convinced me to buy the game in the first place. Very affordable.
This game is definitely worth your money - especially if you're an anime fan.

Saints Row IV, the newest iteration in the action sandbox that broke all the rules. The Third Street Saints have moved from their home in Stilwater, to a media empire in Steelport, and now after being declared national heroes, the Boss has become the President of the United States. But before they get to sit on their laurels, the Zin Empire, a benevolent alien race, decide to take over Earth and put the Saints in a virtual simulation of Steelport.
But enough about that, let's get down to business. The plot follows the Boss and the Saints as they attempt to escape the simulation and overthrow the Zin influence. It is told with that classic Saints Row humor and silliness that we've all come to expect. It is definitely an overly cliched story, but that is part of the fun! So many things waiting around the corner.
The gameplay is mostly the same as SR:TT, but with an alien reskin and a few additions. Most of the missions do feel like filler and fetch quests. The activities are directly borrowed from the previous game. But I tend to forgive the missions for that unique humor and explosive awesomeness.
Length wise, it can take you anywhere from a pretty intense night or a couple days, depending on how you play. Although the folks at Volition love to shower us with as much freedom as possible, sometimes it feels to much, and infact after the main story arc is finished, there is not much to keep you occupied - save for the hundreds of data clusters hidden around the  simulation.
The addition of superpowers makes for a whole lot more fun, but because the map is a carbon copy of Steelport, it can be hard to truly find something new to do. Besides the new alien tech, there is no difference in vehicles or map design between 3 and 4, which is a real let down. The super sprinting and jumping is fun and all, but it just makes Steelport feel a lot smaller than it needs to be.
But no doubt about it, Saints Row has always been about freedom in a massive open world, and that is exactly what you get to do here. The sandbox insanity is still there, as well as the host of unique weapons, vehicles and clothes that characterise it. You get to do whatever your heart desires, and more.
For Saints Row fans, SRIV is already an insta-buy, simply for the insane fun and complete freedom that this game embraces fully. For newcomers however, it would be great to start at Saints Row 2 and work your way up. In summary, if you like shooting aliens in the face, nonstop action and mech suits, then you are going to love this game. Otherwise, it is hard to recommend.
