Fairy Fencer F follows the story of Fang, a scruffy young man in search of his next meal.  He initially gets told about a rumor: the one who can remove the Fury from the ground will have any wish he desires granted.  Through a series of unfortunate events, he gets duped into traveling the world in search of other Furies in order to revive the Goddess.
Personally, the story made me laugh so hard I thought I was coughing up a lung at one point.  The only thing honestly keeping me from giving this a 9/10 is
.
The gameplay is nothing to be too excited about.  At a certain point it's mostly just a bunch of button mashing to either force an avalanche attack or avoid it in order to get through battles faster.
Similar to Hyperdimension Neptunia, your characters start in a formation (which can be edited) and the game creates the turn order based on the AGI stat.  However, unless you use a skill or a magic attack, all attacks are single-target only as opposed to multi-target.
Also, with a system like mine, I should not have frame drop at all and it occurs quite often, either while skipping through text or when loading in a dungeon.  Specs at the bottom of the review for an idea.
From Compile Heart's and Idea Factory's other titles, I was surprised to find the soundtrack within the game files itself, which is part of why I'm giving this a 9/10 (who doesn't like free soundtracks?).  The music during Fairize especially surprised me the first time I heard the tracks.  Other than that, unless I was grinding levels or quests out, the music was always turned on.
If you're like me and try to obsess over achievements, you're guaranteed to get a lot of play time out of this.
Even if you aren't, my first playthrough still ran me 39 hours, short breaks included.  If you go on the general rule of thumb of $1 per hour of gameplay, you're still beating it at full price (although maybe wait for a sale anyway.  It's on sale during all of the major holidays).

First game I'd owned on the Xbox 360 back in 2006 when I was a kid. Kept the very same CD and case until about a month ago, when I'd finally decided to pawn in all the old stuff I'd played. Knew this would be coming out, so I wouldn't miss the game much.
I'm pleasantly surprised at the stability of the game. I clocked in 17.3 hours in a SINGLE SESSION of gameplay, just because I was so addicted to playing the game again. Although the game is improved for PC and looking fine, framerates kinda drop when facing a horde of zeds. Oddly enough, this only really happens outside of the Maintainance Tunnel, so I guess there are a few points of optimization missed during the port. Performance will chug if you find yourself in the middle of particle effects like explosions. From what I've seen, though, mostly everyone can expect decent framerates.
Controls are the same as ever, which will bug anyone that's gotten as used to the newer controls of Dead Rising 2 and so on- particularly the ability to move while aiming a weapon. If you play through with a controller like I have, you'll also be annoyed by the fact that your crosshair will drift further than the slightest nudge you tried to give it to correct your aim. I'm assuming this isn't an issue for anyone using a mouse and keyboard, but just keep in mind that, as I've said before, the controls are the same as ever.
You can't complain much about the graphics, especially given the fact that you can run on resolutions not offered by the 360's hardware. Everything looks sharp unless you zoom in on certain textures with the camera, and you could expect just about the same level of detail as Dead Rising 2 + OTR. Just don't go into this expecting co-op or item combinations.
All in all, this has been worth it. If a game can squeeze me for time all in one go like that, I'd call it a success. Unlike when I was a little kid and too intimidated to go very far into the game because late-game difficulty always seemed like such a grown-up thing to tackle, I've gotten used to and even enjoy challenge in games now. To top it off, I have a lot of experience in wading through this game's difficulties in the past, so some of the tricks I'd long forgotten ended up resurfacing mid-game in a satisfying way.
Grab this game, especially if you haven't played anything earlier than DR2. The story and atmosphere of the first are superior to the later entries, especially given the tone put off when faced with psychopath conflicts and the deaths of certain characters. You'll feel for the events of this game far more than the unserious nature of the others.

TL;DR: 8/10 If you think you'll like this and want to buy it, don't. Buy advent dark force, if you are hesitant about or don't like JRPGS, this won't change your mind.
Kind of dissapointed I bought this one since advent dark force was on sale as well and I could've gotten that :(
The story is preety good. Some of the characters will grow on you, and some you'll learn to hate while others you will not care for. However be careful which characters you begin to like and use as your main force in battle because hearing them shouting the same 3-4 lines in combat will make you hate them preety freaking fast.
Speaking of, the combat is a turn based active combat system, which means you take control of one of your units, walk up to the enemy, do some button pressing, to either just mash the buttons and deal a bit of damage or make combos using launchers and pursues to deal a bit of damage with a cherry on it. If you play on medium or above difficulty you will like come across a steep difficulty curve in the latter part of the game, which means that you haven't grinded enough. I almost got my party whiped twice at 2 specific points where I didn't understand why the enemies were so tanky. At first you might think that you should split your party, having one ranged and 2 melee, a tank, a dps and a healer but don't bother, the enemies attack randomly and using abilities is just pointless, the mana bars empty faster than mcdonald's on a "everything is 90% off" day. take my advice and just get 2 melee and 1 ranged pure physical combo gods. Max out their combos and physical damage and give them launchers and purusers attacks. That's the best I've found so far. Also just keep Fang in your team, he becomes very powerfull, very quickly. The combat also has this "tansformation" Thing where you can, after taking or dealing a bit of damage, have a big song and dance after which the character puts on some new clothes and gains bonuses to stats and access to a special ability that takes 40% of their total HP and a bit of mana to perform. But aside form 1 specific character which is really good, I haven't been using these abilities since a good old combo to the face does the job most of the time.
The graphics are nothing to write home about. Late ps2, early ps3 era graphics with simple dungeon design that won't force your brain a lot. There's a bit of platforming in the dungeons but nothing too hard. Weather this simplistic design works to it's advantage or not is up to personal prefrence, really.
As to what really grinds my gears is that I can't skip the fairization animation (or at least I don't think you can, I haven't dug deep into the config menu to see if you can or not) or the animation for the ultimate abilities and after casting each around 100 times they really start to weigh on my enjoyment. Also, I'm not really sure how the magic system really works, I maxed out one character's magic damage and took all it's abilities and cast them but they were mere specks of damage to the enemies meanwhile combos took at least half of any normal enemies HP bar and took less time to cast.
But regardless, if you are looking for a traditional jrpg to play just for the nostalgia of playing a jrpg similar to the early final fantasies but with a more updated and simplified combat and upgrade system and ps2 graphics then you should REALLY buy Advent dark force, otherwise if you want to experience how Fairy Fencer F was before advent dark force, though I don't know why you would, then this game is for you, otherwise if you don't like jrpgs or are unsure of them, don't bother.
This is a difficult game but it's actually pretty cool. Hope to see more from these guys.

I did have some issues with the game, mainly I'd estimate half my deaths were due to bugs or controls- or as I like to referance 'Dark Souls 2 Deaths." (Being in Dark Souls, you feel you earned the death and that it was a difficult challenge you overcome- however in Dark souls 2 they feel...cheap.)
I will also say, the last level of the game has the best (and worst) level design and parkour elements of a game I've ever seen. One moment I'm free flowing like I've never seen capable in a video game before, and the next I'm falling to my death from a point that looks 100% reachable, but for some stupid reason the game says it's not.
Now regardless of the story, or the length, or the redunancy of searching for items, (I'd forgotten for 80% of the game that there was a hot button to show what you can search. Just to give you an example of how often I did search.)
the Killing of zombies...is fun. Sorta. In the begining it's great and you feel like a badass. This is coming from a person who has played it for the first time ever in 2016, never owning the original on the Xbox 360.
I must say, the day I heard this is coming to PC I was exhilarated. Having played all the other available titles on PC (2, OTR, 3) I believe this one is the best in the series.
For starters, the first entry in the franchise was developed by the core japanese team of Capcom. Japanese humor and quirks are noticable here and there, and some cutscenes feel that way. It's not bad nor obnoxious though. It's what made this game fun and memorable back in 2006. It has its own charm. It feels and plays very differently from the ones made by Capcom Vancouver (2 and onwards).
I think I'll pass on reviewing all aspects of the game as much more professional reviews are available from when the game was released, instead I will focus on the port quality.
My experience with the port was flawless. I have used only keyboard and mouse controls which I found to be easy to use and comfortable, but skill moves might be tricky to initiate at first. The camera movement needs some time to get used to, as it feels like you're dragging it around. That "effect" can only be disabled for aiming, sadly. There seems to be no negative mouse acceleration either, which plagued other entries in the series on PC, but even on max sensitivity the camera might turn a bit too slow for someone.
Eventually one can get used to it, and doing swift movements becomes second nature.
I haven't stumbled upon any gamebreaking bugs either, which really made me happy.
Game supports 4k resolution, MSAA up to x8, uncapped frame rate, a motion blur toggle, and fully rebindable controls, so most needs will be satisfied.
Now the bad things, because this game is not THAT perfect.
There is a feature called "hitstop", which freezes the game intentionally on one frame when hitting zombies with blunt weapons. It was supposed to enhance the impact of blunt weapons, but for many it can be jarring, especially running at a significantly higher framerate than it was designed for. The effect itself amplifies the more you hit in one swing, making it appear like your game completely freezes for a second if you charge into a group with a bench. Luckily mods will be available soon so it's likely it can be modded out.
Even though I haven't experienced any bugs doesn't mean they don't exist. There are multiple reports of the game not launching at all due to lack of a specific Windows update, no audio issues which are apparently fixed by updating Internet Explorer, or higher framerates resulting in more damage taken, even allowing the player to be one shotted. The team is aware of those issues and as far as I know, they're working on fixing them. Apparently those are mostly occuring on Windows 7.
I was lucky enough to not suffer from those issues.
There's also the problem of the game's infamous really stupid survivor AI. It's so annoyingly dumb that it can make you want to throw your computer out of the window. Just be aware that escorting survivors back to safety will raise your blood pressure.
In summary, I dare say this is a high quality port, probably the best Dead Rising PC port that exists in this franchise. I want to thank Capcom for going forward with decision to allow Dead Rising 1 to reach current generation consoles and Q-LOC for doing excellent work on the port. I believe the original experience from 2006 is available here, right now. For 20 bucks you can too cover wars, you know.

First off I want to say that I desperately wanted to recommend and like this game. On the surface it combines CCG elements, real time strategy and skill. All things that I SHOULD like. However, once you actually play the game for a while you ultimately come to the conclusion that strategy/skill has little impact on the experience and it’s nothing more than a RNG grind.
In short progression works as follows. Each character needs to be leveled up both in raw level and also in the skill tree. Neither of these tasks takes that long which is nice. However, then each character has multiple equipment slots which need to be outfitted. Many of the equipment items will come in parts, so you'll need multiple parts (5 for example) to make one full equip able item. Items are then upgradable in level as well. Items are bound to the character so you cannot unequip them without losing it. And then if this wasn’t enough characters can be "+'ed" to increase the stats with shards. All of this lends to a massive investment in one character in both time and materials. Now this actually self-defeats the strategy element. Since you'll likely invest in a main squad of 4 you are essentially locked into your static strategy every time.
Furthermore, there is no point in manually playing vs auto if you are going to be grinding over and over and over. So you end up just autoplaying ever encounter on fast speed just to get them over with.
Avoid this title unless you are looking for a idle game.

Okay, so I gave the remake a good, honest try that extended past the hour of bull hooey on Danny's computer....
I won't bother going over an exhaustive list of the differences between the two games because honestly, the remake is different enough to warrant being its own game *inspired* by the original. The premise is the same, the missions are nice, but I don't think that it's either fair (or possible) for the remake to 'stand up' against the original-- simply put, I don't think that a younger audience would be able to deal with the old interface, graphics, and flat-out-butt-kickin'-nonsense that was XCOM: UFO Defense.
A couple of key notes here:
1) The class base system is nice but almost completely random. You'll find yourself particularly attracted to some, not liking others, and winding up with a mixed bag of both. The game does absolutely nothing to help here, making you purchase rookies like they're going out of style to find the right grab bag of combinations that you want. A mixed squad of the base classes *can* be nice, but only if you play a certain way.
2) This is no longer the nuanced 'laser or plasma' debate: flat out, plasma wins because laser needs to be reloaded. Don't ask, don't tell-- the younger generation is going to miss out on all of that. Maybe even for the best.
3) The tutorial will run you on rails so hard you'll check for scorch marks in your crotch. You have been warned.
4) Stats? What stats? The class base system overrides stats so completely you'll never notice them, randomized or no.
5) The game is trying to tell a story, a sequential story which can be exploited. Unless you're playing the tutorial, in which case, enjoy hell.
6) The game has limited the strategic elements of the game and has narrowed it down to a tactical level. Nice, if you like that kind of game. Far less grand strategy (if you could even say that of the original) because all of your things are in a single base with a well-thought out, fairly streamlined interface.
7) For those of you who want to complain about ammo management: they did it, it's done, it's not bad. You have to reload WAY more often than in the original but it adds a tactical dimension not otherwise noticed (except for those who played small-squad games).
8) For those who want to complain about reaction skill removal: overwatch is a great mechanic and actually makes sense to those who couldn't/didn't/wouldn't do the math from the original. Dumbed-down isn't always stupid, it's functional.
9) For those who want to complain about the interceptions: no person in their right mind played a game that deliberately required them to send up multiple Interceptors who didn't lose before the first year. Yeah, it's not as hardcore as the original, see 8.
10) For those who want to complain about the inability to purchase certain items, *cough*personnel*cough*, etc etc: it makes the plot decisions more interesting.
All in all Firaxis has done a great job re-envisioning XCom. It's fun, it's fast, and it's not even close. 8/10

A refreshingly designed puzzle game which is at its core a match-3 but which has more than enough variation and expansion on that core concept to not be just casually placed into the same genre without thought. If you're getting a Candy Crush vibe from the screenshots then you're on the right track, but instead of having to clear the entire screen by matching gems you're just creating a path for your mage to reach the end. Along the way you'll gain power-ups which perform certain actions, and encounter enemies which wander around the map generally being a pain by adding further obstruction to your attempts to reach the end which you can kill by matching gems on them or by using the relevant power-up. You also have various obstruction blocks which require you to match them more than once, or match certain colours nearby to fill a meter in them, and so on.
Generally each level thankfully lacks that feeling you'll get in other match-3 games where it seems like you're at the mercy of the starting random gem placement and more that you could conceivably reach the end on the first try by judicious use of the power-ups that you're given for completing levels and by thinking ahead as much as the visible play area will allow. There's a story about some mages and why they're freeing some caged fairies each level but this isn't a Phillip K. D.ick adaptation it's a wrapper to give some agency to why you're traversing a level which you can only advance through by matching gems to clear a path.
It's also nice to see a mobile game ported to PC which not only removes its IAPs but which also alters the game mechanics and difficulty appropriately to ensure that you're not troubled by a grind or otherwise frustration which would have been an attempt to get you to either buy the game (reasonable) or purchase power-ups (ala Candy Crush, which is unreasonable). I honestly don't know which this column this game sat in on mobile, I'm just aware that it was announced that the mobile IAPs would be removed for the PC release. You're given random power-ups to place onto any given level (randomly) as you progress, and if nothing else when you do inevitably have to retry a level you're at least treated to an adorably irritated mage who throws her (or his) wand to the ground in disgust.
If this game appeals at all then you should at least give the demo a shot and see what you think, and if ten bucks seems on the high side then it would appear that during the many sales that occur on Steam they apply a 50% discount so it's definitely worth a closer look.

TL;DR:
Rescue Quest Gold is definitely thumbs up if you really enjoy a challenging match 3 game. It can be fun and frustrating at the same time if you are OCD like me. This review is based on 27.2 hours of play time. After finishing 111 of 200+ levels, my average is about 15 minutes per level (long for a match 3). However, many levels I replayed over and over to try for 3 stars and 2 of them I still have only 2 stars (110 & 111).
PROS:
1.	plays in a window with mouse only (wheel zooms board in and out)
2.	excellent voice acting, cut scenes and story (though minimal)
3.	colorful graphics
4.	clear a path to cages so spritelings can be released
5.	ability to manually drag board around to see or play on different areas
6.	map (bottom right) can be used to see the layout and where keys, monsters, etc are located
7.	addictive (can also be a CON)
8.	1-3 stars for level completion
9.	200+ levels (CON for me since I was only able to complete 111)
10.	replaying levels keeps the highest star rating even if it is not the latest
11.	Steam trading cards
12.	59 decent Steam achievements
13.	fast response from active developers regarding problems & “bugs”
CONS:
1.	"number of moves" match 3 except for “races” which are unlimited moves
2.	no RELAXED difficulty mode; only normal play mode and some EXPERT levels if unlocked
3.	breakable tile colors are similar to each other and some backgrounds making it difficult to tell what is cleared and what is not
4.	some tokens are close in shape and color making it hard to tell which is which (especially when the board is zoomed out); pink, red & purple are especially close
5.	winning levels depend too much on luck; on difficult levels if “good tokens” are not on board right off the bat, restarting to try for better tokens is best
6.	One of four SPECIAL EFFECTS (power-ups) awarded after completing a level; when used, three of the four are placed randomly on the board and more often than not placed where they can’t be used and/or are not that helpful
7.	not all SPELLS (another group of power-ups) can be used in every level
8.	Most levels cannot be completed without using SPELLS and/or SPECIAL EFFECTS
9.	dragging the board when zoomed all the way out does not always “stick” where placed
10.	spider webs make it difficult to tell what the token is underneath the web making it almost mandatory to go by shape alone and even sometimes that is difficult
11.	 “dark” levels are just too dark and very frustrating
12.	requires a minimum of 1 star to open cages
13.	star system is backward from most games I have played (bar goes up instead of down; starts with 0 stars and goes up to 3 stars but final tally depends on how many points were made in the level AND how many moves are left at the end AND releasing the spritelings so you can be close to 3 stars but may or may not get the third one depending on the actual end of the level; very frustrating when getting to the top but just under the 3-star line
14.	MAGIC DART SPELL did not seem to work all that great in some levels; especially the BROODMOTHER level
15.	hovering over monsters (especially in BROODMOTHER) is slow to show tokens underneath
16.	cannot go to next level unless current level is finished successfully
17.	when SPECIAL EFFECTS that were awarded from previous levels are used and the level failed or is prematurely ended, SPECIAL EFFECTS used are not returned
18.	Some bugs required closing and opening the game to fix and/or contacting support
All in all, I enjoyed playing the game for as far as I got. I would have preferred to be able to finish all 200+ levels but it just became too frustrating for me. A RELAXED mode would have helped tremendously.

This one's a bit odd.
It's almost like a mobile match-3 game. It has a colourful, well-drawn map. It has colourful, well drawn game graphics. The basic game mechanics are there. And it's oddly addictive. But the developers seem to have gone a bit off-message in a few places...
For example, there are the usual bonus power-ups, but you
Like, wtf? Also, they seem to have missed the lives counter and timer off the display for some reason (noobs), although this doesn't seem to have effected play so far. There wasn't the obligatory pay wall at about level 15 either. In fact the whole of the fisrt section is available as a 'demo' which then asks you to buy the 'full' game to continue. For an insane amount, given this is essentially a mobile match-3 game.
In addition to these schoolboy errors, they also seem to have provided a few (I'm only at level 37 so far) innovative ideas which are actually quite fun. And the whole thing seems well optimized, runs totally fluidly, and so far hasn't crashed. You can even zoom in/out with the mouse wheel.
Come on, developers! What on earth were you thinking?!?!
Seriously though, this game rejects the business model that many (myself included) have despised for years now; the horrid IAPs. By offering a solid demo and charging a fixed amount to unlock the game without limitations, they have given us
what we have been asking for.
So obviously, a solid recommendation from me, on that grounds alone. If you are a casual gamer, get this game. Even if you're not a massive fan of match-3. You'll have the fuzzy warm feeling of supporting a developer who has decided to ignore the convention which has come so close to killing the casual games market for many. (It's also a rather good match-3 game, btw.)

Repetitive, but what it repeats is very highly distilled, polished, high quality chaotic shooting, although good teamwork can temper the chaos and it feels good when teamwork allows you to get a handle on the situation. Despite surface level repetition and merely modest content variety the game held my interest for nearly 40 hours, and I still sporadically play it. I can't see it regularly holding anyone's attention for more than my 40 hour mark, but if you like frantic shooters you'll always have the urge once in awhile to hop on for a quick bit of carnage.
The gore and general feedbback for damaging enemies is fantastic, even if such things for larger enemies aren't as dynamic as the smaller ones. The graphics are great and save for activating the enthusiast "NVIDIA Flex" Physx powered super gore effects (physics based fluid blood and entrails!) the game is quite easy to run. The attention to detail on the weapons are insane (as a gun nut this may thrill me more than most) as the animations are smoothly recorded at over 200fps to allow absolutely smoothness even during periodic slow motion bouts (caused by a system that kicks bullet time at admittedly unclear points when someome does something impressive).
Overall not the most varied game but the difficulty and teamwork give it surprising depth and it is fun in the most classic sense of a videogame, where you can jump on for simple bouts of self contained gameplay sessions, have some fast entertainement, maybe bring in some friends for some company, and be done in as little as 20 minutes if you wish.

I haven't played many match-3 games lately but the art for Rescue Quest Gold caught my eye. It's bright and colorful, and the game is divided into different areas with their own themes so there's always something new to look at. It's pretty challenging unlike Bejeweled but definitely less frustrating than Candy Crush. There are objectives per level to reach the cage, get keys, or defeat enemies. They say the path-based mechanic adds a bit of strategy, but I think it's pretty straightforward and not overcomplicated. There's a mix of easy and hard levels so you don't get bored easily. You also get powerups and spells to use, and it takes some practice to figure out which ones to solve specific levels. I was extremely excited when I saw the previews coming out for Dying Light and having just beaten the main storyline I felt the need to share that the game lived up to even more than I had expected.  The story overall was enjoyable and far more in-depth than your standard zombie game.  It had its twists and turns and, as a huge zombie fan, I can say that it definitely brought some new elements to the genre.
The combination of the open world and the parkour results in a very fun traveling experience especially after you've leveled up your Agility path and gained some special techniques to go along with it (like leap frogging over zombies, using a long-range grappling gun, and being able to run up a flat surface for a short distance).  I don't recall having played a game where I enjoyed traveling from Point A to Point B so much.
In addition to the Agility path, you are able to level up your Survivor and Power paths.  Survivor gives you the ability to make chemical boosts and grenades, cover yourself in zombie guts to sneak by other zombies, and craft shields out of materials that you've scavenged along the way, among plenty of other unique passive and active skills.  Power is the fighting-based path which gives you additional abilities to use with your weapons. as well as enhacing their effects overall.
As for the most memorable aspects of the gameplay, the day and night cycle plays a massive role in Dying Light.  I found myself literally afraid to be out at night as the areas outside of safe zones were FAR more dangerous than they had been during the day.  Also of note is the crafting system which is basically an improved version of what was found in Dead Island - scavenge materials and craft grenades, medicine, tools, etc. and use those same materials to MacGyver your own unique weapons, like a baseball bat with nails (simple) to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sword that carries a strong electrical current and light enemies on fire (insane).
This is the Skyrim for zombie fans.  I highly recommend this to fans of zombies, RPGs, open worlds packed full of side quests, and parkour!

Well I've finished the main campaign and collected most of the achievements so I figure it's a good time to write a review of the game.
First What I liked.
The free movement and open world concept while still keeping some areas out of reach until later in the game was very nice. Not setting up the quests so that any level player could win it at any time was wonderful. I very much liked the death penalty. It punished you for making mistakes yet did it without causing you to lose forward progress on the collectables or skill progression. The game world in general had a nicely random feel, much like I would expect from a city that grew slowly over a long period of time.
Most of the main story arc and nearly all of the side quests were fun and interesting. And the characters were generally believable and engaging enough to accommodate the situation.
Combat was fluid and dynamic with many skills being quite fun to use at all points in my play through.
The main quest story was well done but unimaginative. The voice acting was good.(I did note that many of the male voices sounded as though they were the same guy that did the high elf in Skyrim)
Many of the side quests and several parts of the main story were exceptionally intense(The final tunnel run being the most nightmare inspiring)
Now what I did not like.
Right out of the gate after finishing very few quests with no feel for the controls nor the general layout of the area you are force to travel halfway across the city during the night while way too many super zombies are milling around everywhere. That one quest part was the most anti logical and disappointing part of the main story arc. Not because it was too hard, I was rather hard but it was obviously completable but because it was completely contrary to the message given by the main theme of the game. You are constantly told to find a safe house and wait until morning yet in the second mission you are forced to leave a safe place if you have managed to make it to one and travel at night with more volatiles around than at nearly any other point in the game. And having to repeat the same jump and run way too many times until I found the “Right” path to make it back to the main safe tower was not fun, it was not exciting, it was tedious and annoying and almost enough to make me uninstall the game. In other words is was an epic fail for the story, at least in my opinion.
The lock picking mini game. It was simple sure, but after picking untold numbers of locks it became so tedious that I finally just modded the mini game file to bypass the need. It would have been much better to have it skill based so that locks below the skill of the player would be auto picked and the player could decide to pick those of a higher level.
The screen effects. Generally the lighting and look of the game was quite well done but one area that failed horribly is the effect applied to the player in various instances. Does the main character not know how to blink for gods sake? When I climb out of the water I can blink a few times and see perfectly fine. I don't spend the next several minutes looking through what appeared to be frosted glass in game. Also Camouflage is supposed to hide you from the enemy NOT hide every thing in the game world from you, Plus WHY would the main character wipe zombie goo in his eyes SERIOUSLY WTF? A timer for the camouflage effect, like those for the drinks, would have been tons better. I really hated the effect with a passion.
In several instances we were forced to deal with distasteful persons and absolute louts. Not once were we given the option to KEEL THEM ALL!!! Even when they had no bearing on any future part of the story.  If someone were to send me on a wild goose chase to get an item for an emergency and then I discovered it was because they wanted to get hammered, I would so kill them dead. Also Crane is a moron for sure.
The “Special” zombies: If there was one thing I could change about Dying light is would be the mutations. Zombies that spit goo for hundreds of meters that will blind you and do damage no matter where is hits anywhere around you. It even blinds you when it explodes behind you. WHY?
A zombie that explodes with the force of a half pound of C4. WHAT?
A zombie the size of a large truck that can take one hundred rounds from an AR-15, in the head no less, and still fight just fine. SERIOUSLY? Also firearms are WAY, so very WAY underpowered. And the shotgun is all but useless.
I would much rather have seen more of the faster normal human size zombies come out at night and the slow walker become more robust when the sun sets. Make the regular zombies more lethal rather than trying to “Amp it up” with completely unrealistic zombie creatures. The fear generated by zombies is not so much from their individual strength but from the knowledge that they are relentless and when in large groups they can become a wave of flesh chewing slaughter.
And finally The one thing I hated most stridently of any part of the game was the absolutely horrible “You have to listen to the antagonist diatribe six thousand times until you get the button mash(a la Dragons Lair) sequence exactly correct and hit every button at the perfect time” finale. I have a melee weapon that does more than 1500 damage and an AR-15 rifle with 100 rounds. I WOULD NOT stand about listening to the nut job blather on about his motivations and desires, I WOULD SHOOT HIM IN THE HEAD!! A LOT!!! Or possibly use my sword as a rectal probe until he grows a shiny horn.
Over all it is a fun game and with the promise of new content in the near future I would certainly recommend it to anyone that likes the heavy action based games. Though if you're looking for intellectual stimulation run away from dying light. Dying Light is a full on MONGO SMASH ZOMBIES romp, parkour style
One caveat: The first few levels of progression will be an awful and tedious grind before you can really start to have fun in Harran.

The Saints are back! Well, sort of. Fans of the first 3 Saints games may be in for a bit of a surprise, that is either going to impress them, or send them into a fit of rage. While other Saints games have been no stranger to going way out into left field, the 4th entry into this series seems to push the envelope even further. So far in fact that it seems like a completely new genre entry into the series. I'm sure by now you know the gist of the game. The gist is that you are no longer tied the laws of normal physics. Why? You progressively and eventually achieve becoming a mother #$%@ing superhero! Oh, and did I mention you are also the President of the United States? Yeah, from just a gangbanger, to a man in tights! Or whwtaever you want to wear to be honest.
Saints Row completely flips the script of previous Saints games, and has you now instead of fighting rival gangs, taking on a legion of aliens bent on destroying everything you care about. You'll meet familiar faces from the past, and run and gun or jump (over buildings mind you) and pound the ground with a bevy of your closest friends from the Saints universe. And Keith David too!
Yeah, you can run at lightning speeds, jump long distances, use telekinetic powers, and a lot more. The melee fighting is a lot better, but still a little lacking. However, punches go hard this time, so it's a lot more satisfying. Like punching a car, and seeing it knocked back quite a distance. You still get guns and other weapons (and LOTS of skins for them). And the way the game flows in combat, you'll find yourself mixing it up with all assortments of moves. Mainly due to limited ammo, and a meter for combat superpowers. This way you're not just spamming one thing over and over again. This makes for some fast and furious action, and I love it!
As far as traveling goes, you do get vehicles. But with how fast you can move in the game, they almost feel like an afterthought. That is of course for aerial vehicles, which can still be useful. This being because while you can jump super high, or launch yourself very far, and even glide long distances, you still never get the ability to fly.
As for the lack of interest in using vehicles which most people find not necessary, the game features the ability to listen to your favorite radio stations usually found in the vehicles, now outside of the vehicles at any time. And this my friends, is quite the dream. The soundtrack has some choice tunes, featuring a wide assortment of genres, and throwback classics. I was floored when I ran into a pack of alien enemies, and "The Touch" by Stan Bush started playing. It made me feel...well...It made me feel like a bad♥♥♥♥♥ The cheesy 80's centric music blaring while I'm zooming in and out of these enemies, using super powers, and feeling like a god. I loved every minute of that. And it was purely by chance. Just some good timing is all.
But not to worry, Saints IV makes good use of scripted badassery, with some fantastic main story missions that are well played out, so it's not all by chance. The story is cheesy goodness dripping with gooey satisfaction. It's never at any moment meant to be taken seriously, and for that I am thankful. This is a game with 1 focus in mind. Having some of the most balls to the wall fun imaginable.
The game however seems like it is over too soon. And honestly, there is not much in terms of challenge. The post game stuff will just leaving you typing up any loose ends for achievements and other odds and ends, but you will pretty much have all side missions complete by the end, and in a short time. So this leaves any post game missions down to any expansion packs we may get for the game. But regardless of length, you will enjoy every minute of it gun toting superheroes with political ties is your sort of thing :D
Pros
- Varied and satisfying gameplay
- Wonderfully scripted main story missions
- Fantastic soundtrack
- Radio stations can be listened to on foot (and in the air!)
- Feel like a complete badass!
Cons
- Game is too short
- Easy gameplay

I never played this game when it came out on the consoles, so this review is made without all of the nostalgia and fanboy fawning that the vast majority of reviews here seem to have. It was probably good back in its day, but it does not hold up as a modern PC game. Reasons are:
1. The game is Nintendo Hard. It uses save points (vomit), and the save points are few and far between, and often require killing dozens, if not hundreds of enemies to reach them. You can easily lose hours of progress trying to get to a save point. Everything is timed, and you sometimes are not given tutorials until AFTER you needed to do something, there are things you will never get right the first time, making it necessary to restart from your last save and lose hours because you did not know a needed gameplay mechanic ahead of time.
2. The AI of your allies is terrible. You have to escort characters back to the saferoom, but if you don't give them a weapon, they wait til you get about 50 feet away and run straight toward you, usually right into zombies, OR if you give them a weapon they go full Leeroy Jenkins and charge at the enemy zombies, and get swarmed.
3. The gun system is terrible. Not only are they impossibly weak, but they are all auto-aim, and there's no way to know what your character will shoot at. A zombie could be two feet from you and you'll shoot the gun only to hit an enemy standing 15 feet behind it. And unless you are on flat, level ground shooting at a target on the same elevation, the AI will not recognize the enemy and not shoot at it.
4. Under some circumstances, enemy respawns are nearly instantaneous. You can kill 30 zombies, walk ten feet past them, and get attacked from behind because 10 more spawned in as soon as you took the camera off of their location.
Overall, the gameplay is fun, but there are simply too many frustrating and unnecessary 'features' artificially increasing the difficulty to make it fun for a PC gamer.

First thing we can notice is that the game is (was) designed for mobile use. But everything works fine with the mouse. The only thing I don't like with the mouse is the camera movement , this should be better on mobile.

Like I said , we're in front of a mobile game but what is really great is that we don't have the downsides of those games. I mean , there's no micro-transaction , you don't have to wait for lives. You can play whenever you want and that is pretty great.
For now I've done 25 levels and some were already tough or maybe I'm just bad at these kind of games lol. However there's something that can be really annoying : music. I only heard one music so far.
Finally, I'd like to say that this game is a good one, the fact that there's no mobile games ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t is a good point allowing players to play at their own pace.

In short: It's a fun little game. Definitely one of the better ones on my list.
By no means is it perfect, but it has plenty of charms going for it.
Good:
I liked how fluid and easy the combat system is. Punches, kicks, slices, bashes, and magic bolts all flow into each other well in what is, essentially, a free form combo system. Smack enemies around however you want using an array of acquired skills and special moves; primarily with the goal of locking enemies into painful juggle combos and smashing them into the hordes for group damage. It is quite satisfying to high kick an enemy into the air, use a Ether Saber uppercut, and then Reverse Spin kick them backwards into the row of enemies behind you.
There are also some rpg aspects there; but it's not really developed. You get experience and 'level up' but it's not all that noticable. You do however get to buy upgrades and equip new special skills and passive skills to change your style and tweak your game. A fair variety of magic attacks, melee skills, and useful passives lets you come up with quite a few interesitng combinations, and with the free form combo system included it's hard to imagine the sheer number of attack patterns and strategies at your disposal.
It's a good challenge too! Surprisngly difficult and unforgiving at times for such a cute theme. Bosses have a whole repertoire of special moves that they can play on random, and are quite capable of keeping up with the agile little fairy brawler. Hordes of faceless mobs will pummel you to the ground, shoot you mercilessly, and all together are quite capable of overwhelming the heroine and knocking her out in seconds. It's a game you have to stay on your toes with.
The music is also good and plays well to the different settings. There is also some japanese voice acting, so that's cool I guess?
And the game is cute. Freesia's a sweetheart to be sure. But if you aren't into anime stuff then there's not much story or lore going on anyways. Cutscenes are pretty barebones with still graphics and text that are overall pretty short, with in game animated scenes lasting only a second or two. Everything else is pretty much left up to the player's imagination. Characters are kind of interesting in personality and design, but you really don't see enough of them to make it count. It's overall standard anime/fantasy story stuff, and that works for me.
Bad:
The game is painfully short. Can be beaten in under an hour if you're fast. Maybe two or three hours on the higher difficulties where you'll be taking your time. For such a sweet and well developed game, it ends quickly and becomes repetitive soon after; albiet still quite amusing.
Repetitiveness is the main problem here. It's not terrible, but defintely the weakest point in this game. There are only five main arenas to fight on, and only four enemy types(short, tall, flying, and giant). Some enemies develop into sub-species with alternate attacks, but for most of the game you'll be facing hordes of the same four faceless enemies again and again. It doesn't help that the first boss is just a bulked up version of a regular enemy as well (thankfully the remaining human boss fights are much more diverse).
There is also a sort of endless quest mode, called 'Guardian Mode', that has you try to fight for 99 levels of randomly selected waves, but that's even more repetitive.  Sometimes I ended up clearing a level only to fight the exact same lvel setup right after; there's not even much variety in the randomized stages!
It is a little slow in the beginning too, when you don't have any basic skills upgraded (and with the first boss not really being that hard), you're stuck using the same moves over and over, and it's easy to get a bad first impression for the game. Things don't start getting interesting until the second arena, but with the game being as short as it is that is a huge minus.
But with the lack of diversity in the challenges aside, it's still a pretty fun game.
Overall: I would have liked a little more variety and challenge, and maybe even a little more story as this game is quite charming despite being relatively simple.  The rpg mechanics could have been a bit more interesting too, but I won't exactly criticize that.
It's a simple beat-em-up about a cute fairy trying to save her tree that features a pretty awesome free form combo system that lets you smash around enemies and tear apart hordes of faceless golems in whatever fashion you want. Despite it's cute theme and repetitive challenges, it is quite difficult and quite fun to play. A "can pick up and finish in an hour" short, but still good fun while it lasts. There are multiple difficulties, plenty of skills to master and try out, a new game+ mode, and an endless mode too if you want a little extra fairy fighting action.
It's just plain fun, and cute as a button to boot. I recommend it, especially for the low price. If you like beat 'em ups then there's no reason not to give this one a swing.

Update: I nominated this game for the "Test of Time" Steam award. The brilliant simplicity of this game lends itself to those sudden "I should play that again" moments. It can only take a few minutes to bring the hexagon's ways back to your mind, and I find its one of those games where I find myself looking to give it another go every once in awhile.
-----
There's an order to the chaos, and when you find it... sheer brilliance. Super Hexagon may look like another twitch-reflex, infinite-play game but there's a method to the madness. Rarely, if ever, is it the game's fault when you lose (though it can certainly feel that way early in the learning process.) As you begin to recognize the patterns and tricks of the hexagon and slowly start to overcome it second by precious second, those seconds can suddenly start adding up to 30 minute (or more) play sessions. The superb music certainly helps too.
No major flaws I feel that need to be pointed out... mainly because I can't think of many flaws to begin with. Its one of those rare games, it seems, that I can really just get lost in. Incredible gem of a game!

+ So much fun when playing with friends! It may not look like much, but the gameplay is an absolute joy. One person drives the truck, while the other person lays down the track from a top-down perspective. You really have to communicate and work together to try to make it as far as you can.

A Twitch friend (PBRGamer) and I had a ton of fun with this for a few hours last night. Fun challenge with friends
Excercise in good communication
Plenty of Customization
No lag even with my bad internet
Easy to pick up
Low file size and low on resources to run
I would like to see some unlockables and such as far as the design stuff goes, as well as vehicles. Unlockables are usually a thing that gives a game a long lasting appeal to me. PBR and I would also like to see an easier way to change positions with your partner, as right now it appeared the only way to do it was leaving the game and starting a new one. Not a big deal, but a small quality of life upgrade.
Thanks to Pixel Maniacs for this opportunity. We look forward to seeing where this goes.

Dying Light: Basically Dead Island gone right as many of these reviews probably already say. The story itself has a couple cliche moments but not enough to make the story predictable. There are a good amount of plot twists and parts that are honestly very sad when you realise what is happening.
Overall I would rate it:
8/10 Singleplayer
10/10 Multiplayer
Seriously, the addition of Co-op was probably the best thing this game has.
My friend personally gives it:
7/10 Singleplayer
10/10 Multiplayer
We have gotten a full enjoyment of the game and I can say that all these hours I've spent in this game are well worth it.

Some Annoying flaws, but Dead Rising is one of my all time favorite video games, hands down.
Dead Rising was originaly released as an Xbox 360 exclusive, and this game was one of the reasons why i got a 360 in the first place.
The premace is pretty simple. you are Frank West, a photojouralist tipped off about somthing big that happened in willament colorado. as it turns out its infested with zombies, and you basically have to survive 3 whole days while uncovering exactly what happened. hence your purpose for going there.
Gameplay is fun as all hell. there are tons of weapons to find and experament with, and there are ALOT of zombies to kill. Bosses in the game are refered to you as Psychopaths, and they provide a great change of pace to the gameplay, aswell as a good window into how people have adapted to life in this insane scenario.
You progress through the game through leveling up VIA Progression Points. you earn these for taking  awesome pictures with your camera, Killing things, defeating psychopaths, and saving civilians from the chaos in the mall.
Visually, this game is extremely impressive considering it came out in 2006. the enviroment looks and feels like a mall, and the zombies look scary and dead. the game runs extremely well, even during points where zombies are almost completely cluttering the screen.
The most annoying things i find with this game are the civilian AI and on some occasions the camera can be a little wonkey.
In my honest opinion this game is a timeless classic and is well deserving of your time

The object is simple; navigate from your starting position to the goal. Getting to the goal is of course the name of the game, and there are plenty of challenges keeping the player form it. The game is heavy on trial and error, at least up front. Once I got used to what I was dealing with like knowing what those pesky red circles did, or how they worked with red walls, I could figure out what to avoid or what to expect, not that it made some of the later stages considerably difficult.
Minimalist design goes over well here. The levels, obstacles, and player avatar are very minimally designed; the colors look like the basic RGB colors. There is nothing flashy at all about the presentation. The background music is nice, plenty of variety, but nothing that will stand out.
The controls took some getting used to, but I didn't have a big problem with them for the most part. I used a game pad but there were times my input to “Restart” a level were not recognized and I had to mouse click and grab the game pad very quickly again. There were also some odd graphical and game play bugs. Pausing for a few seconds on a stage with deadly red particles then resuming would cause the particles to rain down in a wall of death.
Another issue is that some of the red walls may be passed on some stages, but not on others, making things feel a bit inconsistent, though as mentioned trial and error is part of the experience, and losing isn't harshly punished as the player gets infinite lives without any real penalty.
If I have any further complaints they would be largely niggling ones. I wish the game was a little more visually flashier, giving things a truly “neon” shine. I wish the background tones were adjusted in some areas as it would occasionally become easy in a tricky move to lose myself in the floating nebulae, which in some cases caused me to retry. Again, these are trivial complaints.
With plenty of stages, and some ambiguous timings on winning stars (or “medals”) for completing stages faster, Neon Space has a lot to offer for a buck. I enjoyed myself, this really felt a bit like a classic arcade style game from the 80s. Maybe a vector mode would have been cool, who knows?

This is one of those games that (assuming you like this kind of stuff) you start to enjoy more and more the longer you play. At the start, you've only got one pretty generic character and a handful of items that will randomly spawn for you when you open treasure chests. As you play the game and unlock more achievements, however, you open up a cast of characters that include the bow and arrow-wielding Huntress, the punch-happy robot called "HAN-D", and more. Playing on different types of characters also allows you to unlock more items by completing character-specific achievements. Along with all this, there's a few different artifacts that radically change gameplay rules that can be found on various levels. (For those of you that hate the random items factor, one of these lets you pick which items you're given from chests!)
Each item and monster in this game also has a sort of lore page that you can acquire either from picking up the item for the first time or killing enough monsters to drop a monster log. None of these are particularly long, but some are pretty funny and they're a nice little detail to add to the game. The music is also very well done and the composer responds pretty frequently to comments on his youtube page.
One thing to note is that the levels aren't randomly generated. Each tier of levels picks a level from a specific area, meaning at some point you'll see all the levels the game has to offer. This doesn't bother me, but it might be a deal breaker for some people. Along with that, if you extend your runs through the game past a certain point, you'll have so many weapons firing off particles that the game can slow down and possibly crash on you. If you only do a run or two through the levels before challenging the final boss though, you should be fine.
Anyways, I think this is a great game that I play whenever I need something quick and enjoyable.

Freesia is a fairy, and her job is protecting Lita Forest.  How does she do so, you ask?  Why, by beating the everlasting crap out of everything that threatens it, of course!
It's an arena beat-em-up, basically.  Between levels you get to the store and purchase skills, level them up, customize your skill set, and more.  The end result being that you can have Freesia beat the everlasting crap out of everything that threatens Lita Forest exactly how you want her to.
The game's graphics are simple, colorful, and effective.  The music compliments the game well.  The controls (at least, the gamepad controls) are fully customizable.  There's also humor to be had, both in the game and its achievement list.
Story Mode itself is fairly short, but you unlock Guardian Mode after beating it the first time, which plays similarly to the Survival Mode present in many fighting games.
The only glaring issue is the difficulty spike better known as the third boss, Shynie.  This is generally when you discover how abusable the invulnerability frames on the backdash are.  You'll eventually get into the rhythm of backdashing through her attacks, getting off a short combo, closing the distance, and repeating the process.
Overall, it's a fun way to spend some time, and definitely worth picking up.  If in doubt, well, there's a demo you can try.  It gives you the first five "days", which encompasses the tutorial and the first boss.  It doesn't sound like much, but it's enough to know whether or not you'll like it.

The premise is simple enough, one stick moves, one strick aims and you have a shot, super shot(that charges pretty quickly), a dash, and a phase.  When you are phasing you are totally invincible but you cannot damage enemies so you will phase through bullets and have to phase back in in order to damage the enemies.
Each level is decently long, roughly 20-25 minutes and have several bosses with an end boss consisting of several phases.  I enjoyed my short time with this game, but I cannot recommend it because of one simple fatal flaw:  no save feature.  The game has 5 levels, the 2 I played each took about 25 minutes, so assuming you don't die(and assuming all levels are roughly the same length) you could beat the game in roughly 2 hours.  I did not know there was no save feature when I started, so I played campaign, beat the first level and went off to do other things.
I came back later, hit campaign and was put back to level 1, I noticed there was a level select option so I checked that out.  Level 1 and 2 were unlocked, no big deal, I figured I could start at level 2 and go from there.  So I select level 2, play through the whole thing and upon beating the level I am put back in the level select screen with nothing else unlocked.  At that point I lost all desire to play this game.
This is 2017, there is no excuse to not have a save feature in a game like this.  I played the game for about an hour, did not die once, and all of that progress just seems wasted.

FTL is a long series of dice rolls that is well camoflauged by fun and surprisingly deep game mechanics. The ship-to-ship battles are great fun with some deceptively powerful tools at the player's disposal. You're well-rewarded for building a good ship and crew, but you are at the mercy of the RNG. The game's main flaw is that your overall game success far too often rides on the result of a 50/50 coin flip for the outcome of an event rather than player skill during ship combat. Losing a crew member to an event that might also gain you a crew member is a risk you simply must take to overcome the punishing boss fight, and it's very hard to come back from a bad luck deficit. You'll eventually find yourself in a rut of exploring as many stars as you can and crossing your fingers for the right chain of good outcomes to beat the game.

Curator Review: Can't Drive This is insane, chaotic, and exciting in the best way. Silly and cute, it is a hilariously good time.
The premise is simple: one person builds the road while another person tries to drive on it. This sounds easy enough. However, the person who is driving has to maintain a constant speed and this eventually leads to hectic road building and chaotic driving. The builder only gets new pieces as the driver covers more distance and going backwards hurts the score. There will be a point in time where you are building pieces right underneath the driver's tires. To make things even crazier, there are trap pieces of road. Dodge wrecking balls, windmills, speed bumps, and more while trying to just stay on course. Luckily, the controls are easy to use and understand, being both responsive and simple.
The only thing I didn't like about the game was the limited soundtrack. While the music that is playing is good it can get annoyingly repetitious after a short while. Taking into account this is early access, I would hope there will be more music added to the game later to help make this game a longer lasting playing experience.
For the future, I hope for more game modes, more players, and a test track for practicing driving.
This game is available as a local co-op, online co-op, or a random matchup with other players online so it is great for every type of set-up. No matter your set-up, the game is spilt screen so you can always see both perspectives. This comes into play on certain trap pieces where it will splash the screen for both players, increasing the difficulty.
Can't Drive This takes simple gameplay and turns it into a game that anybody can play and have an absolute blast! In the video below, we had to stop playing at one point because my compatriot was laughing too hard at the sillyness that had befallen us in the game. She doesn't play too many different video games but she thoroughly enjoyed this experience.

Let's be honest, you look at this game and what do you think?  Probably something like: hey, that looks cute, probably fun for a couple of hours but not really something I'd buy.
This game is by no means perfect, but it is AWESOME.  When I think of things to compare it to, I think games like Super Smash Bros. or the classic Pole Position.  It's just the most hype inducing, focus requiring, shout inspiring, frustrating game ever.  It looks easy enough, "oh, I'll just drive slow."  Nope.  "I'll just go straight."  You're funny.  "How bout I just throw away this piece." Good luck with that.
While there are legit strategies, there is no way around it.  This game is all about quick thinking, reflexes, and communication.  It's the kind of game that has you shouting and getting super frustrated but also super happy when you beat a personal record.
The gameplay is amazing.  I spent most of my time so far playing with a friend online, but I did play a few public matches as well.  It is the kind of game that is way more fun with a friend.  However, since it is setup with local split screen you have the setup for a hillarious living room game session with friends.  And you may think, "ew split screen."  But the game is split screen no matter what (even nonlocal), because you need to see what your partner is doing.
So while this games does a lot right, it does a lot of others not so great.  This game's central focus relies on connectivity being on point so if there are any problems you're screwed.  Any latency, toast.  I'm not sure what can really be done about it, but we had several games end because of lag and a few matches where we just completely disconnected.  It sucks that the core element of this game means any connection issue is your ruin.
Also, the music is ok... like what is there sounds good, but there's like 2 songs.  It is very repetitive.  More tracks are needed ASAP.
Gameplay/mechanics wise the only bad thing is it is almost impossible to recover from a trap.  Like if you hit a bell, it is impossible to straighten your car out mid air.  Also I kind of wish the different car models had sort of different specs to them for another layer of strategy.
Overall it is a fun game.  It has the potential for hours of hillarious, intense, dramatic fun.  Just turn off the music and play local if you can.  I give it an 8/10.

Antichamber is a puzzle game, but if you're looking for something you think of when you think of those words you should probably look elsewhere. At its core, the actual puzzles of Antichamber are a series of relatively simple puzzles where you use blocks to open doors, create paths to walk on, and other various things, and they're all pretty easy unless you just aren't doing things in the right order and don't realize that you don't have the right block gun upgrade to do that puzzle or haven't realized that you can do a certain thing with a certain block gun. The challenge comes in the form of the environment itself, which was presumably designed with a "Beginner's Guide to Non-Euclidean Geometry" in one hand at all times. The only hard part of the game is actually getting from one puzzle to the next without falling into a pit that materializes under your feet or being stuck walking up a staircase that appears when you walk on it and having to exit back to the lobby and try again. It's fairly one-trick and isn't likely to fool you for very long, unless you plan on searching for the optional secrets like the pink cubes. Overall Antichamber isn't a horrible game, but it's not a game that I would really recommend. If you're new to the concept of non-euclidian geometry then it might get a few "oohs" or "ahhs" from you when it tries its parlor tricks, but if you've played The Stanley Parable you've already seen most of what this game has up its sleeves and you'll probably just end up bored even before you finish what is a pretty short game.

I am unsure on how to start with this review, the game does so many things in a transparent, simple surface design intention in both story and gameplay mechanics to a point where it would seem like a terrible game on paper. Yet, after fully completing the game, I would argue otherwise!
(By the way, completing the game is pure insanity. Thus I would suggest you refrain from even having that slight idea on this game or any other title from the same studio!)
people tend to compare this game with another title by the same studio due to their similar mechanics, the Hyperdimension series. I will not be doing that, instead I will try to judge this game as it is. Also, again I state, even though most of what I say here will probably sound unappealing, check on the bottom of the review for there I will try to justify why I believe that is not the case.
Story: (Might contain spoilers)
All JPRGs have a storyline. Some are good, others are horrendous. This one is leaning towards the bad, unfortunately. It is basically just "There is a goddess of good and a god of evil, they both are in a state of hibernation. We must revive the goddess of good by collecting some stuff and so on!" You can basically tell where this is going by now. There is nothing that interesting about the story and it is rather transparent to be frank.
Most of the story is presented in a Visual Novel fashion of storytelling. If you have played a visual novel before you would immediately understand what I am referring to. If not, however, it is basically just showing a 2D picture of a character whom is supposed to be conversating, with animated mouth movement and maybe the occasional one hand raising up, and that is it. It was intentional to have the story be a Visual Novel, but it felt lazy in a way. Also, there are only a hand full of 3D animated cutscenes, so yeah...
Characters:
One of the strong points of this game, yet not strong enough to compete with other titles, I dare say. Since this is a JRPG you would expect a large party of characters, and you are correct. except, in terms of character development, only three are affected. And the rest are just there. When inspecting each character individually, they are all one-dimensional. Each one has just one unique trait and personality, that is it. Yet when together, the interactions and dialogue are truly great! I do like the comedic side of this game and how these one-dimensional characters were able to bring that sense of comedy to life.
I won't explain character traits here. But believe me, one look at a given character says it all.
Overworld:
There isn't much to speak of here. the overworld is basically menus with pretty pictures. In town, you click the button on screen to access the inn, shop, whatever. world exploring is just looking over a map and choosing a place to go to and you instantly teleport there. That place you went to is where the game is. As in, where you can move freely and do your combat and whatnot. Unfortunately, even though these places can be forests and deserts, but when carefully looking, it is your typical standard dungeon. In other words, gameplay is only shown in dungeons.
There is one pleasant thing about the world map, though. You have the option of stabbing swords on the ground (Sounds odd, I know) to gain some buffs into the dungeons you wish to visit. Example, stab a sword that grants bonus exp but reduced defense next to dungeon "X" and there you go!
Mechanics:
very few commands when exploring. There is movement, press "B" to jump, press "A" to attack/interact. As for combat mechanics. It is a turn based battle in 3D. Your character has a small space for you to position him/her. After choosing, you pick his/her action. Whether it be basic attacks, magic or status elements.
The game does a huge plus by introducing a fusion mechanic at the beginning of the game. Hooking that player fairly early. As for difficulty, the game is very easy. So easy, in fact, that I did not bother with learning combos until maybe a few quests prior to finishing the game’s storyline.
Music:
There aren’t much. But for what there is, it is rather pleasant. I do like most of the songs in the game. Maybe two or three I would consider listening to outside of the game. And to the game’s credit, the songs in some way does fit the aesthetics.
Visuals:
3D Graphics are slightly higher than a regular PS2 game. Visual Novel art is pretty. Nothing more to that.
Overall:
Critically, this game does almost everything averagely. and that will disappoint so many people. But it is that very reason why I loved this game. It is Average with good character interactions! With all the newly released games and their "Super amazing next gen gameplay mechanics!" and whatnot, it was very relieving to have a game that you can just enjoy without putting much effort into it, Plus the combat was easy. Thus, it was overall a very relaxing experience for me!
I do hope that I was able convey my point in this review.

Please read more than the first few lines since there is a good deal to this game and it is not a clear yes or no.
So i have set the review as recommanded because i recommand YOU try it out yourself first.
So first of: would I recommend the game?
Yes and no. it is a fine time waster for very little time sessions if you just want to be a F2P player, but if you want to play long sessions and invest time in it I would say "properly not" because of how it stops you from playing in long sessions.
the reason is not that it is a bad game, I actually ENJOYED it a lot. But that to enjoy it in its fullest or for longer periods in one session, it will be excessively expensive.
The play time without paying is around 15-45minutes of play-session(15min if you played that day and done everything, 45 if it’s the first time of the day and you take your time with everything), then you have to wait for 4hours before you got enough “hope” (currency that drain when playing) to play again.
You can pay to get past this, but this will cost you around 2$ per 1hour to play which is too much for me.
On top of that, everything that gives good rewards are soft paywallet, meaning after x runs you need to pay to keep doing that activity.
Now if we ignore the payment system, or if you don’t mind the pricing. (we know devs got to eat and some people find this kind of payment system perfectly fine; just for me the play-sessions are too short and too expensive in the long run to keep playing. )
It is actually a really nice and solid game. With a lot of fun to be had.
The game have good graphics for what it is.
Sounds is pleasant if you like sound on the game.
The ability to have automatic combat is awesome, it makes the game
There is a vast variation of creatures to use and a high amount of skills to assemble.
Now this is a very nice touch, the issue with it is that the stats difference on gold cards to silver and normal is so huge then anything that isn’t gold (besides the first healer, because it takes forever to get a gold healer) isn’t worth using or upgrading. This limits your variations very much.
To get gold cards you generally have to buy them, why it isn’t too bad and for around 100$ you can get a pretty decent card deck. To get gold card without an initial investment is very hard, due to the best way of getting them besides that is events where only the best players (those with the best deck) gets the full cards. This means if you haven’t made an initial investment you will be very unlikely to get them (it can be done).
The same goes for the arena and island (both places you can get points to buy gold cards).
Now the issue with this is not that your accumulation is slow, but that you are VERY limited to how  much you can accumulate each day (unless you pay as mentioned.).
There is a ton of upgrading of creatures so there is LOTS of progression for each creature.
The nice thing about this is that the good creatures you will feel get continually stronger and that you have a lot to evolve on them.
The bad thing is that the difference on a fully evolved and a new creature is like night and day, we are talking 1 shotting entire teams vs. getting 1 shotted very easily. This means again that only cards with high upgrading is worth taking, and since it takes a LOONG time for this unless you pay your way to victory, you will feel annoyed of how big the difference is.
Every creatures got skills that can be upgraded, and it takes time and ingame ressources, the ingame ressources for this is accumulated at an acceptable rate for upgrading (at least until lvl 9-10 upgrades) and the upgrade is time based and take x hours to complete, which is a nice system (you can buy your way past this wait as well).
You can buy extra skill slots for a reasonable price (rl money) and if you will play the game a lot I will advise you to buy at least a couple of extra slots, since these are permanent and fair priced.
Now one of the things I found the most pleasant with the game is the ability to manage the creatures, and then have it automatically fight the battle’s while I lean back and enjoy the carnage. This is an awesome feature and the ai for this is pretty ok (healing usage of skills could be better though hehe.) The only issue I see with this is the before mentioned difference in power spikes which for most fights means it is very one way. :)
Improvements I would love to see is:
Unlimited hope, maybe a way to get arena tickets from normal fights as well. Unlimited hope would mean you could play as much as you wanted but still only get a limited amount of progress since all the best stuff are limited other than the hope system. (the rest of the pay systems are ok, devs have to make money somehow)
A little bit better ai on auto combat. (mostly on the healer skill use, so they don’t constantly wasted it)
Tweaking to the stats of none upgraded card to fully upgrade. So we don’t see 1000%+ increases, but closer to 100%+- from no upgrades to max. To allow for a lot more diversity in card use.

The devs are very nice, understanding and helpful. I would not be afraid putting my money with them.
Personally I got mislead by the shop because the information isn’t good in it (BEWARE: shop info +hope is not maximum hope, it is limited uses of potions that gives 50hope per potion, and royalty system rewards skyrocket in amount you need to invest, at 100$ you will be at lvl 5, at 200$ lvl 6 and I can’t even imagine how much from there :P hehe. I bought in with the mistake thinking otherwise then I just stated and the dev team helped me get a full refund (and closed my account, which is only fair and was discussed before they did anyhting).
Now anyone that have used steam a lot knows how IMPOSSIBLE it is to get refunds on steam, so a team getting steam to give a full refund is VERY rare and to me it proofs the best of intention from the dev team.
So major props to the dev team for that. Proofing that if you want to invest with them, they are fair about it and will refund if it is a reasonable request. So you can invest with them with a relaxing mind :)

I would recommend try it out for 1-2weeks if you find that the playsession are of reasonable length (know that before lvl 20+- you lvl pretty fast and therefore get a lot of extra hope, so it is not representative of playsessions length in higher lvls. That’s why 1-2 weeks) then consider buying into it.
It is a very nice and fun game, and if not for the short play-sessions and lack of ability to increase the max hope to a high amount the game would be worth investing a lot of time in.
