Fun game, but there is no difficulty slider and eventually you end up just playing it for the story and not for the gameplay.
Exploring dungeons is pointless, there's nothing to look at (graphics are console/outdated), nothing to explore too. You're better off going in a straight line to the objective in every dungeon instead of looking for loot/monsters to kill. Side quests are practically worthless, rewards are ok but when you literally stomp every enemy your level (and then some) you don't really need to be careful when playing. For perspective, I had to play against enemies 2x my level to even get a sort of challenge, since I couldn't roflstomp enemy mobs then. So don't buy it for the gameplay.
Story wise though it was fun. Funny to play through, has funny little bits of trivia that you can pick up while you're in town by other civilians, though those interactions are just going to a menu (kinda) and selecting characters to talk to.
Ignoring the side stories, the main storyline is quite enjoyable. Only "problem" would be that it's not particularly deep in terms of character development, but that's irrelevant since it's pretty much a casual game to enjoy for say... 14 hours or so.
Characters also have weird challenges that you could grind if you wanted to, but those seem to be put in for those who wish to punish themselves. Like "jump 10, 50, 100, 2000, 5000 times in a dungeon with <x> character". And the reward for completing more and more jumps/attacks/whatever doesn't stack well, so eh.
7/10, worth getting on sale. Not sure about full price though, since I'm fine with spending 7.99 for what I got, but full price of $30 is a bit much. I really would've liked a bit more depth to gameplay/story for more fun, but it's ok as it is.
Buy on sale (like all games), grab the additional dlcs (get the ultimate armor pack to enjoy the OP playstyle faster), could skip the cosmetic sets though.

When you were a child, did you ever wonder about how your adult life would be? Having grand aspirations on becoming something more than your  parents were, following your own path in life and trying to enjoy yourself within the best of your ability. You would pack a lunch that you made yourself, or if you had lunch tickets that would have to satiate your appetite until the next day, because your family was too poor to offer you any type of sustenance.
No when you came home, it was usually to a house of yelling and throwing things, your mom could have been a junkie your dad an alcoholic and the many brothers and sisters you have, were all so ♥♥♥♥ up beyond belief, they were never home. Your mom could have various men over to feed her habit, and sometimes these men would molest you, and so would your father after a stupor. This type of child had no chance in life. These children are brought into the world to do nothing but suffer. They play escapism in their minds to ease the pain that they are in. The only remedy for them would be to take them out of that hostile environment and place them with a truly kind family.
Child 1 would exhibit some issues, but for the most part he would live a pretty decent life, giving the fact he/she would have the social skills and the support that they need to push on through. If not brought up properly they would proceed to become entitled and have this persisting narcissistic personality disorder. Nothing would ever be enough and everything that bad ever happened would be others fault.  So while both children would have these things in their minds growing up, child 1 for the most part would be extremely more likely to succeed instead of child 2, who would developed a multitude of mental illnesses, where they couldn't cope with for the rest of their lives.
I have witnessed both of these things growing up, while attending school. You could always tell the children who were damaged and the children that had a pretty much life of leisure. I fall somewhere between child 1 and child 2, a mixture of real bad♥♥♥♥♥♥ and real good♥♥♥♥♥♥ A loving home, but also a broken home. A sheltered childhood, rampant with violence and chaos outside, filled with children growing up way to fast, and running dope on the street, like it's some sort of normalcy for them. My house was filled with a lot of fighting, arguing and general malignancy from many family members. A loving mother, grandmother and aunt, protecting me from the harms of the real world and the neighborhood. I spent most of my childhood indoors in front of the TV playing video games that my mom or grandmother would rent for me at blockbuster, I had a five dollar a week allowance that I could spend on whatever I wanted.
We were very poor, but we always had the lights on, food on the table, and a roof over our heads. My mother and grandmother would buy me the latest consoles even if I had to wait a bit, they would put layaway's and surprise me at birthdays and Christmas, my mom would write little sayings in my book bag for valentines day saying how much she loved me, and my grandmother would always cooked what I wanted for thanksgiving and Christmas. I had many good memories and many bad memories, but these three women always tried within the best of their ability to always make sure that I was always taking care of. I always had new clothes throughout the school year, and I always use to go to parks with my aunt because as said earlier the neighborhood was too bad to venture outside. I was hated throughout elementary school because I wasn't like most children. I use to get terrorized on the bus and made fun of because my hobbies included listening to music and playing video games. I was picked on for being overweight, and for being to proper and respectful.  Teachers were always antagonistic towards me, because I was the kid always questioning things, as to make them feel like it's more work for them, as oppose to enlightening a young mind.
I would go through middle school and high school pretending to be something I am not. I would dress in my own style that consisted over various name brand clothing, I would always get the latest shoes  and colognes and I would put of this mask of someone who is wealthy and happy. I gave my mom and grandmother a lot of stress during this time, we didn't have the money to keep up this image and I would get into fights with them about it. I was popular, I hung out with people who made quadruple my mothers income, they would ride around in Mercedes and BMW, while my mom had this rinkydink Buick from the late 80s. I was ashamed of her jobs that she took to support me, and ashamed of where I lived and the cars that my family had. I tried everything to the best of my ability to make sure no one found out. I was loved, people knew who I was, they wanted to be me, they wanted to be able to be what I was. Girls were actually intimidated by me, come to find out later on, the reason I had such a hard time dating was because of the fact that these girls didn't think I would take it seriously and feared rejection.
I'm not tooting my own horn, I began to hate what I have become, what I was, what I was turning into. It was fake, I was a fraud, I was everything every kid wanted to be in middle school and high school, but I was horribly depressed. Until one day I couldn't take it anymore, and It caught up to me. In the middle of high school I had an immunity disorder, for some unknown reason I would get sick every week. I missed more than a 120 days of school. I had bronchitis, mono, flu, strep, pulled groin, dislocated knee, walking pneumonia, I had it ♥♥♥♥ing all. During this time my grades were awful, I mean they always were terrible, but they really tanked. A little after summer, and after 9/11 I didn't attend school, I was majorly depressed and wouldn't leave my room, by this time I moved into a better neighborhood and things were a bit different. Like I said though, I stayed in my room all day and finally I was expelled for missing too many days. That was it, it was over, my so called friends forgot about me, and my popularity meant jackshit. I would suffer from this for an obscene amount of time.
From that point on things didn't get better they just got worse and worse. At the end of 2011 I was hoping for a better year, I've been reclusive and working the job I still work at till this day that I hate, but at the end of 2011 I was hoping that I would finally have a good year, that this is the year that I would make a change. 2012 comes in, off to the same start as any other year, my grandmother had her 75th birthday, and I was as close as ever to her, till late March, where she got sick, she was hospitalized and had two mini strokes and passed away, 2013 would come and my uncle would be hospitalized with the same issues my grandmother had, he would last one more years and die in October of 2014. Every year since 2012 had been the worst years of my life, 2013 was particular horrible, but that's a bit too personal to get into, so lets just say it was just purely awful.
It's 2016 right now, and I am terribly unhappy, and have difficulty living each day. My heart is broken to a million pieces because I miss my grandmother and uncle so ♥♥♥♥ing much. So take it from me, just live life the best you can and share it with others who cherish and deserve your love.

At its core, Killing Floor 2 is a wave based cooperative first person shooter. However, the game and its gunplay are so polished that it can't be helped that it is so addicting at times. The level of detail Tripwire puts into their weapons and the nuances each one displays make killing Zeds extremely satisfying. The variety of different enemies also adds for a more dynamic experience, creating situations where teammates can go from easily holding their corner of the map to ones where they have to regroup with their companions in the face of overwhelming numbers and the appearance of "miniboss" type Zeds. All of this is wrapped up at the final round, where your team is pit up against one of two bosses, each having its own abilities and weaknesses. All in all, if you're looking for a game that emphasizes teamwork, unique and satisfying weapons, and long term support from its developer, Killing Floor 2 is the game for you.

The basis of the game is: You are somewhere where something not-so-great has occured and you are trying to escape while piecing together what has happened.  You are an engineer and can combine inventory items into all sorts of neat stuff.... discovering what can be combined into what is part of the fun.... but surprisingly the combat and atmosphere are OUTSTANDING despite the... somewhat unrefined graphics.  I never buy anything on Steam that isn't on sale but this is one of examples of a game that is fully worth the full asking price.  The DLC is also pretty neat.... it adds a soundtrack (the original game has no music)... but the music must be accessed by the Steam Music player... simply Shift-Tab while in-game and select the soundtrack.  A warning: missing out on the audio cues from enemies can be a disadvantage... but the DLC also adds multiple different starting scenerios.  By this I mean instead of starting out with a 9mm pistol and an extra clip or two you might start with a revolver and extra ammo, or a bunch of dynamite and no gun, or a number of other situations.  It privides much-needed diversity in the very early-stages of the game and forces you to get good at using different weapons and tactics.
In short: Teleglitch is an amazing game that does a lot with 60 megs of data.  It is HARD.... like REALLY REALLY hard but I've had a blast despite never getting past level 7.... I actually died in the very first room on level 7 and died in extreme fashion.  Think Dark Souls-style difficulty mixed with a large helping of Dead Space, all in a top-down environment.  This game just has "it", that Special Sauce that just makes it fun.  I read about this game on RockPaperShotgun and, having learned to trust their opinions, game-wise, decided to give it a chance when I found it on sale.  I'm pretty sure this has been the only game I've played since I bought it aside from a little bit of the Fallout 3/Fallout New Vegas combining Tale of Two Wastelands.  I've started up Teleglitch each of the last couple of days to just play a round or two (you have one life per playthrough... so a "round" would essentially be until you finally die.... which happens quite a bit) but ended up playing for the entire day.  Despite all of my roughly-30 attempts ending in terrible, terrible failure: this game is just a lot of fun.  Way moreso than the sum of it's parts would suggest.

I have played plenty of JRPGs that I can't see too much difference between this game and the others.
Pros :
- Distinct, unique cast of characters, with nice interactions between each character
- Plenty of character's customization such as weapon upgrade, skill upgrade, costumes, etc
- Good combat animation makes the battles less boring
- Good overall soundtrack
- Japanese-English voice option
- Skippable conversation, pretty convenient for those who want to retry the game in NG+ for achievements
- Consistent 60fps
Cons :
- Somehow, the world felt really small. 1 city and 14 different dungeons (not including DLCs). Most dungeons only consist of 2-3 floors/stages. You can easily explore the whole dungeon in just a few minutes
- Boring, uninspired dungeons
- Lack of challenge in combat
- Pretty common, forgettable, short storyline
If you are looking for games where you can enjoy the story and character's interaction, you will enjoy this game.
Overall, I give this game 7/10. It's not the best for its genre, but it's still enjoyable.

This is one of the best Idea Factory RPGs I've ever played since Chaos Wars and Blazing Souls.
I have to admit: Idea Factory's earlier RPGs were enjoyable too, but had too many flaws and unpolished features so that I couldn't recommend any of them as a stand-alone game of a genre. Fairy Fencer F is different in my opinion.
It's a turn-based rpg with a combat similar to Hyperdimension Neptunia Rebirth series and Mugen Souls. If you played those games you'll probably notice many familiar things.
Fairy Fencer actually has a lot more useful and polished features compared to Neptunia Rebirth series. While the game starts off simple, its core gameplay gradually gains more and more stuff. And I'm not talking about just crafting feature or sub-quests. There are unlockable combos, enemy weaknesses, team-attack system, character-unique actions, fairy card bonuses, etc.
Sure there is still quite a few in-game stuff which makes you wonder 'This could've been so much better if you added X', or 'Why did they not exploit this further?', or even 'This system doesn't make much sense.'
But all in all I wouldn't call it a wasted potential.
The game is not the best, but a very solid and enjoyable JRPG in my opinion. I would definitely recommend trying it out.
I also have to mention that Fairy Fencer F has a really good optimization. It runs on my pre-historic dualcore like a charm.

This is THE most F2P/newbie generous TCG as of 2017.
Faeria used to so until they dropped their buy all the cards for a cheap low price.
Now lets get this clear, TCGs in general is not a game best experienced from a F2P position. You just cannot keep up with those who would pay for crystals to get the Shadowverse daily deal for card pack.And then what happens is that you are restricted in the number of deck types you can field. And then those who are in this position will go around grumbling about this and that card/s, deck/s that they don't have being overpowered.
As for aggro, Shadowverse is quite "anti aggro". Instead Shadowverse is orientated towards combo decks and wins are accomplished by steady reduction of hitpoints OR a surprise burst of damage. If you don't like combo generated burst of damage, DON'T start playing Shadowverse where you have only 20 health points and when a combo kicks in, it usually though not necessarily means game over. Its a east vs west culture thing.
Games are thus designed by intention to be short, anything above turn 10 is pretty epic and both are probably playing control.

As for going for face, aggro decks well lets put it this way, you drop 2 or 3 warded minions before turn 4 and typically, aggro Sword or aggo Bat will concede. And there is ample early board clear available. You want to see aggro being supreme, play Faeria as Yellow. You don't even need to harvest mana from the well.
Play a go for face, face is the place type of deck, prepare to be conceding a lot of times.
I used to harvest on ladder/rank the much gripped about Blood Spawn deck (pre nerf) until they nerfed it and my cheese got moved. Now I harvest aggo. :) If you cannot find the gap in the meta, well, go reddit and call for nerfs and say you want to go back to Hearthstone. I dropped Hearthstone because I found that in Shadowverse, it is much cheaper to maintain my status and infinitely more fun. When I get combo-ed/meme, it actually brings a smile on face while swearing... and I promptly go about trying to recreate that deck if it is new to me.
I strongly suggest that if you are going to play Shadowverse, you be prepared to buy a 1200 crystal set each month. USD29.98. This 1200 crystal will allow you to buy 24 packs over a month using the daily offer. Then save the gold you get  from daily task, enough to buy a pack typically, for buying packs from the quarter expansion. Yes there is a new expansion set every 3 months. The extra cards you can from the daily deal, you liquify for vials (crafting resource) and save them for the new expansion. I am typically able to open 150+ new expansion card packs at the start each expansion this way.
Using this strategy, you will have more than enough resources to get all the cards each expansion. And right now there is offer to for newbies to get 7500 crystals are a discounted price and you can get the discounted price for up to 3 purchases.
Also note that Shadowverse ladder system is newbie friendly. Its operates on a leagues model. There 5 ranks/leagues before Master rank. You don't lose you rank each month but you can stop yourself from ranking up to a more competitive rank if you don't have a competitive card collection. And at Master rank, you compete to be in the top 10000 players for vials and 10 free card packs each month.
Card expansion rotation is expected in 2018 so that should limit the initial financial outlay if you are starting now and decide to be serious about the game. Basic card set and maybe 4 expansions will in play each time. Maybe more than 4. And remember, you don't have to decide so soon, there are tonnes for free packs to get just starting the game and from story mode and you will be insulated from a cut throat competitive because of the league/rank laddering system.
I am pretty sure it will be fun assuming you are not going to be F2P, the meta will change each expansion, people will grip about this and that, there will be nerfs, the meta changes again BUT all the while, there will be plenty of opportunities to harvest the "sheep" decks by using the correct techs against the sheep decks or by using one that specifically targets it.
Your ability to analyze and arrive at a solution against "sheep" decks (aka netdecks) will be be rewarded in Shadowverse. Intelligence gets used and gets you the wins.
